lines.text: These nails should rend that beauty from my cheeks.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: These eyes could not endure that beauty’s wrack;

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: You should not blemish it if I stood by.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: As all the world is cheered by the sun,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: So I by that; it is my day, my life.

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: Black night o’ershade thy day, and death thy life.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Curse not thyself, fair creature; thou art both.

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: I would I were, to be revenged on thee.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: It is a quarrel most unnatural,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: To be revenged on him that loveth thee.

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: It is a quarrel just and reasonable,

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: To be revenged on him that killed my husband.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: He that bereft thee, lady, of thy husband,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Did it to help thee to a better husband.

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: His better doth not breathe upon the earth.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: He lives that loves thee better than he could.

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: Name him.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Plantagenet.

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: Why, that was he.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: The selfsame name, but one of better nature.

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: Where is he?

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Here.
[_She spits at him._]

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Why dost thou spit at me?

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: Would it were mortal poison, for thy sake.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Never came poison from so sweet a place.

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: Never hung poison on a fouler toad.

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: Out of my sight! Thou dost infect mine eyes.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Thine eyes, sweet lady, have infected mine.

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: Would they were basilisks to strike thee dead!

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: I would they were, that I might die at once;

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: For now they kill me with a living death.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Those eyes of thine from mine have drawn salt tears,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Shamed their aspects with store of childish drops.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: These eyes, which never shed remorseful tear,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: No, when my father York and Edward wept

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: To hear the piteous moan that Rutland made

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: When black-faced Clifford shook his sword at him;

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Nor when thy warlike father, like a child,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Told the sad story of my father’s death,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And twenty times made pause to sob and weep,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: That all the standers-by had wet their cheeks

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Like trees bedashed with rain. In that sad time

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: My manly eyes did scorn an humble tear;

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And what these sorrows could not thence exhale,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Thy beauty hath, and made them blind with weeping.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: I never sued to friend nor enemy;

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: My tongue could never learn sweet smoothing word;

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: But now thy beauty is proposed my fee,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: My proud heart sues, and prompts my tongue to speak.
[_She looks scornfully at him._]

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Teach not thy lip such scorn; for it was made

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: For kissing, lady, not for such contempt.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: If thy revengeful heart cannot forgive,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Lo, here I lend thee this sharp-pointed sword,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Which if thou please to hide in this true breast

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And let the soul forth that adoreth thee,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: I lay it naked to the deadly stroke,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And humbly beg the death upon my knee,
[_He kneels and lays his breast open; she offers at it with his sword._]

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Nay, do not pause, for I did kill King Henry—

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: But ’twas thy beauty that provoked me.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Nay, now dispatch; ’twas I that stabbed young Edward—

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: But ’twas thy heavenly face that set me on.
[_She falls the sword._]

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Take up the sword again, or take up me.

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: Arise, dissembler. Though I wish thy death,

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: I will not be thy executioner.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Then bid me kill myself, and I will do it.

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: I have already.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: That was in thy rage.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Speak it again, and even with the word,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: This hand, which for thy love did kill thy love,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Shall for thy love kill a far truer love.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: To both their deaths shalt thou be accessary.

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: I would I knew thy heart.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: ’Tis figured in my tongue.

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: I fear me both are false.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Then never was man true.

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: Well, well, put up your sword.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Say then my peace is made.

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: That shalt thou know hereafter.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: But shall I live in hope?

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: All men, I hope, live so.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Vouchsafe to wear this ring.

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: To take is not to give.
[_He places the ring on her hand._]

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Look how my ring encompasseth thy finger;

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Even so thy breast encloseth my poor heart;

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Wear both of them, for both of them are thine.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And if thy poor devoted servant may

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: But beg one favour at thy gracious hand,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Thou dost confirm his happiness for ever.

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: What is it?

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: That it may please you leave these sad designs

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: To him that hath most cause to be a mourner,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And presently repair to Crosby Place;

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Where, after I have solemnly interred

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: At Chertsey monastery this noble King,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And wet his grave with my repentant tears,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: I will with all expedient duty see you.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: For divers unknown reasons, I beseech you,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Grant me this boon.

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: With all my heart, and much it joys me too

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: To see you are become so penitent.

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: Tressel and Berkeley, go along with me.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Bid me farewell.

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: ’Tis more than you deserve;

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: But since you teach me how to flatter you,

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: Imagine I have said farewell already.
[_Exeunt Lady Anne, Tressel and Berkeley._]

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Sirs, take up the corse.

lines.speaker: GENTLEMAN
lines.text: Towards Chertsey, noble lord?

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: No, to White Friars; there attend my coming.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Was ever woman in this humour wooed?

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Was ever woman in this humour won?

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: I’ll have her, but I will not keep her long.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: What, I that killed her husband and his father,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: To take her in her heart’s extremest hate,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: With curses in her mouth, tears in her eyes,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: The bleeding witness of her hatred by,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Having God, her conscience, and these bars against me,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And I no friends to back my suit at all,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: But the plain devil and dissembling looks?

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And yet to win her, all the world to nothing!

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Ha!

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Hath she forgot already that brave prince,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Edward, her lord, whom I, some three months since,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Stabbed in my angry mood at Tewksbury?

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: A sweeter and a lovelier gentleman,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Framed in the prodigality of nature,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Young, valiant, wise, and, no doubt, right royal,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: The spacious world cannot again afford.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And will she yet abase her eyes on me,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: That cropped the golden prime of this sweet prince,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And made her widow to a woeful bed?

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: On me, whose all not equals Edward’s moiety?

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: On me, that halt and am misshapen thus?

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: My dukedom to a beggarly denier,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: I do mistake my person all this while!

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Upon my life, she finds, although I cannot,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Myself to be a marvellous proper man.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: I’ll be at charges for a looking-glass,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And entertain a score or two of tailors

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: To study fashions to adorn my body.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Since I am crept in favour with myself,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: I will maintain it with some little cost.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: But first I’ll turn yon fellow in his grave,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And then return lamenting to my love.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Shine out, fair sun, till I have bought a glass,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: That I may see my shadow as I pass.
[_Exit._]

scenes.setting: London. A Room in the Palace

lines.text: Have patience, madam. There’s no doubt his Majesty

lines.text: Will soon recover his accustomed health.

lines.text: In that you brook it ill, it makes him worse.

lines.text: Therefore, for God’s sake, entertain good comfort,

lines.speaker: GREY
lines.text: And cheer his Grace with quick and merry eyes.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: If he were dead, what would betide on me?

lines.speaker: GREY
lines.text: No other harm but loss of such a lord.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: The loss of such a lord includes all harms.

lines.text: Ah, he is young, and his minority

lines.text: What likelihood of his amendment, lords?

lines.text: Madam, good hope; his Grace speaks cheerfully.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Ay, madam; he desires to make atonement

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Between the Duke of Gloucester and your brothers,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: And between them and my Lord Chamberlain;

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: And sent to warn them to his royal presence.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Would all were well—but that will never be.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: I fear our happiness is at the height.

lines.text: They do me wrong, and I will not endure it!

lines.text: Who is it that complains unto the King

lines.text: That I, forsooth, am stern and love them not?

lines.text: By holy Paul, they love his Grace but lightly

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: That fill his ears with such dissentious rumours.

lines.text: Because I cannot flatter and look fair,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Smile in men’s faces, smooth, deceive, and cog,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Duck with French nods and apish courtesy,

lines.text: I must be held a rancorous enemy.

lines.text: Cannot a plain man live and think no harm,

lines.text: But thus his simple truth must be abused

lines.speaker: RICHARD

lines.text: To who in all this presence speaks your Grace?

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: To thee, that hast nor honesty nor grace.

lines.text: When have I injured thee? When done thee wrong?

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Or thee? Or thee? Or any of your faction?

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: A plague upon you all! His royal Grace,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Whom God preserve better than you would wish,

lines.text: Cannot be quiet scarce a breathing while

lines.text: But you must trouble him with lewd complaints.

lines.text: Brother of Gloucester, you mistake the matter.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: The King, on his own royal disposition,

lines.text: And not provoked by any suitor else,

lines.text: That in your outward action shows itself

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: I cannot tell. The world is grown so bad

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: That wrens make prey where eagles dare not perch.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Since every Jack became a gentleman,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: There’s many a gentle person made a Jack.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Come, come, we know your meaning, brother Gloucester.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: You envy my advancement, and my friends’.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: God grant we never may have need of you.

lines.speaker: RICHARD

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Our brother is imprisoned by your means,

lines.text: Myself disgraced, and the nobility

lines.text: Held in contempt, while great promotions

lines.text: Are daily given to ennoble those

lines.text: Against the Duke of Clarence, but have been

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: An earnest advocate to plead for him.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: My lord, you do me shameful injury

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Falsely to draw me in these vile suspects.

lines.text: You may deny that you were not the mean

lines.text: And then deny her aiding hand therein,

lines.text: My lord of Gloucester, in those busy days

lines.text: As little joy, my lord, as you suppose

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: You should enjoy, were you this country’s king,

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: As little joy you may suppose in me

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: That I enjoy, being the Queen thereof.
[_Aside._]

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: As little joy enjoys the Queen thereof,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: For I am she, and altogether joyless.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: I can no longer hold me patient.
[_Coming forward._]

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Hear me, you wrangling pirates, that fall out

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: In sharing that which you have pilled from me!

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Which of you trembles not that looks on me?

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: If not, that I am Queen, you bow like subjects,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Yet that, by you deposed, you quake like rebels.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Ah, gentle villain, do not turn away.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Foul wrinkled witch, what mak’st thou in my sight?

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: But repetition of what thou hast marred.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: That will I make before I let thee go.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Wert thou not banished on pain of death?

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: I was, but I do find more pain in banishment

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Than death can yield me here by my abode.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: A husband and a son thou ow’st to me;

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And thou a kingdom; all of you, allegiance.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: This sorrow that I have by right is yours;

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And all the pleasures you usurp are mine.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: The curse my noble father laid on thee

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: When thou didst crown his warlike brows with paper,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And with thy scorns drew’st rivers from his eyes,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And then to dry them, gav’st the Duke a clout

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Steeped in the faultless blood of pretty Rutland—

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: His curses then, from bitterness of soul

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Denounced against thee, are all fall’n upon thee,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And God, not we, hath plagued thy bloody deed.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: So just is God, to right the innocent.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: O, ’twas the foulest deed to slay that babe,

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: And the most merciless that e’er was heard of.

lines.speaker: RIVERS
lines.text: Tyrants themselves wept when it was reported.

lines.speaker: DORSET
lines.text: No man but prophesied revenge for it.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Northumberland, then present, wept to see it.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: What, were you snarling all before I came,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Ready to catch each other by the throat,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And turn you all your hatred now on me?

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Did York’s dread curse prevail so much with heaven

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: That Henry’s death, my lovely Edward’s death,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Their kingdom’s loss, my woeful banishment,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Should all but answer for that peevish brat?

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Can curses pierce the clouds and enter heaven?

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Why then, give way, dull clouds, to my quick curses!

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Though not by war, by surfeit die your King,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: As ours by murder, to make him a king.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Edward thy son, that now is Prince of Wales,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: For Edward our son, that was Prince of Wales,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Die in his youth by like untimely violence.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Thyself a queen, for me that was a queen,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Outlive thy glory, like my wretched self.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Long mayst thou live to wail thy children’s death,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And see another, as I see thee now,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Decked in thy rights, as thou art stalled in mine;

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Long die thy happy days before thy death,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And, after many lengthened hours of grief,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Die neither mother, wife, nor England’s Queen.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Rivers and Dorset, you were standers-by,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And so wast thou, Lord Hastings, when my son

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Was stabbed with bloody daggers. God, I pray Him,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: That none of you may live his natural age,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: But by some unlooked accident cut off.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Have done thy charm, thou hateful withered hag.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And leave out thee? Stay, dog, for thou shalt hear me.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: If heaven have any grievous plague in store

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Exceeding those that I can wish upon thee,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: O, let them keep it till thy sins be ripe,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And then hurl down their indignation

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: On thee, the troubler of the poor world’s peace.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: The worm of conscience still begnaw thy soul;

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Thy friends suspect for traitors while thou liv’st,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And take deep traitors for thy dearest friends;

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: No sleep close up that deadly eye of thine,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Unless it be while some tormenting dream

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Affrights thee with a hell of ugly devils.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Thou elvish-marked, abortive, rooting hog,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Thou that wast sealed in thy nativity

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: The slave of nature and the son of hell;

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Thou slander of thy heavy mother’s womb,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Thou loathed issue of thy father’s loins,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Thou rag of honour, thou detested—

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Margaret.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Richard!

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Ha?

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: I call thee not.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: I cry thee mercy then, for I did think

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: That thou hadst called me all these bitter names.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Why, so I did, but looked for no reply.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: O, let me make the period to my curse!

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: ’Tis done by me, and ends in “Margaret”.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Thus have you breathed your curse against yourself.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Poor painted queen, vain flourish of my fortune,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Why strew’st thou sugar on that bottled spider,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Whose deadly web ensnareth thee about?

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Fool, fool; thou whet’st a knife to kill thyself.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: The day will come that thou shalt wish for me

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: To help thee curse this poisonous bunch-backed toad.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: False-boding woman, end thy frantic curse,

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: Lest to thy harm thou move our patience.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Foul shame upon you, you have all moved mine.

lines.speaker: RIVERS
lines.text: Were you well served, you would be taught your duty.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: To serve me well, you all should do me duty:

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Teach me to be your queen, and you my subjects.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: O, serve me well, and teach yourselves that duty!

lines.speaker: DORSET
lines.text: Dispute not with her; she is lunatic.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Peace, Master Marquess, you are malapert.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Your fire-new stamp of honour is scarce current.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: O, that your young nobility could judge

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: What ’twere to lose it and be miserable!

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: They that stand high have many blasts to shake them,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And if they fall they dash themselves to pieces.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Good counsel, marry. Learn it, learn it, Marquess.

lines.speaker: DORSET
lines.text: It touches you, my lord, as much as me.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Ay, and much more; but I was born so high.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Our aery buildeth in the cedar’s top,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And dallies with the wind, and scorns the sun.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And turns the sun to shade, alas, alas!

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Witness my son, now in the shade of death,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Whose bright out-shining beams thy cloudy wrath

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Hath in eternal darkness folded up.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Your aery buildeth in our aery’s nest.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: O God, that seest it, do not suffer it!

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: As it is won with blood, lost be it so.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Peace, peace, for shame, if not for charity.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Urge neither charity nor shame to me.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Uncharitably with me have you dealt,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And shamefully my hopes by you are butchered.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: My charity is outrage, life my shame,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And in that shame still live my sorrow’s rage.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Have done, have done.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: O princely Buckingham, I’ll kiss thy hand

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: In sign of league and amity with thee.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Now fair befall thee and thy noble house!

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Thy garments are not spotted with our blood,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Nor thou within the compass of my curse.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Nor no one here, for curses never pass

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: The lips of those that breathe them in the air.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: I will not think but they ascend the sky,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And there awake God’s gentle sleeping peace.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: O Buckingham, take heed of yonder dog!

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Look when he fawns, he bites; and when he bites,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: His venom tooth will rankle to the death.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Have not to do with him; beware of him;

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Sin, death, and hell have set their marks on him,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And all their ministers attend on him.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: What doth she say, my lord of Buckingham?

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Nothing that I respect, my gracious lord.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: What, dost thou scorn me for my gentle counsel,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And soothe the devil that I warn thee from?

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: O, but remember this another day,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: When he shall split thy very heart with sorrow,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And say, poor Margaret was a prophetess.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Live each of you the subjects to his hate,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And he to yours, and all of you to God’s!
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: My hair doth stand on end to hear her curses.

lines.speaker: RIVERS
lines.text: And so doth mine. I muse why she’s at liberty.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: I cannot blame her. By God’s holy mother,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: She hath had too much wrong; and I repent

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: My part thereof that I have done to her.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: I never did her any, to my knowledge.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Yet you have all the vantage of her wrong.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: I was too hot to do somebody good

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: That is too cold in thinking of it now.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Marry, as for Clarence, he is well repaid;

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: He is franked up to fatting for his pains.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: God pardon them that are the cause thereof.

lines.speaker: RIVERS
lines.text: A virtuous and a Christian-like conclusion,

lines.speaker: RIVERS
lines.text: To pray for them that have done scathe to us.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: So do I ever—(_Speaks to himself_) being well advised;

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: For had I cursed now, I had cursed myself.
Enter Catesby.

lines.speaker: CATESBY
lines.text: Madam, his Majesty doth call for you,

lines.speaker: CATESBY
lines.text: And for your Grace, and you, my gracious lords.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Catesby, I come. Lords, will you go with me?

lines.speaker: RIVERS
lines.text: We wait upon your Grace.
[_Exeunt all but Richard._]

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: I do the wrong, and first begin to brawl.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: The secret mischiefs that I set abroach

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: I lay unto the grievous charge of others.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Clarence, whom I indeed have cast in darkness,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: I do beweep to many simple gulls,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Namely, to Derby, Hastings, Buckingham;

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And tell them ’tis the Queen and her allies

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: That stir the King against the Duke my brother.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Now they believe it, and withal whet me

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: To be revenged on Rivers, Dorset, Grey.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: But then I sigh, and, with a piece of Scripture,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Tell them that God bids us do good for evil;

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And thus I clothe my naked villany

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: With odd old ends stol’n forth of Holy Writ,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And seem a saint when most I play the devil.
Enter two Murderers.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: But soft, here come my executioners.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: How now, my hardy, stout, resolved mates;

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Are you now going to dispatch this thing?

lines.speaker: FIRST MURDERER
lines.text: We are, my lord, and come to have the warrant,

lines.speaker: FIRST MURDERER
lines.text: That we may be admitted where he is.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Well thought upon; I have it here about me.
[_Gives the warrant._]

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: When you have done, repair to Crosby Place.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: But, sirs, be sudden in the execution,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Withal obdurate, do not hear him plead;

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: For Clarence is well-spoken, and perhaps

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: May move your hearts to pity, if you mark him.

lines.speaker: SECOND MURDERER
lines.text: Tut, tut, my lord, we will not stand to prate.

lines.speaker: SECOND MURDERER
lines.text: Talkers are no good doers. Be assured

lines.speaker: SECOND MURDERER
lines.text: We go to use our hands, and not our tongues.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Your eyes drop millstones when fools’ eyes fall tears.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: I like you, lads. About your business straight.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Go, go, dispatch.

lines.speaker: BOTH MURDERERS
lines.text: We will, my noble lord.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: London. A Room in the Tower

lines.text: Enter Clarence and Keeper.

lines.speaker: KEEPER
lines.text: Why looks your Grace so heavily today?

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: O, I have passed a miserable night,

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: So full of fearful dreams, of ugly sights,

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: That, as I am a Christian faithful man,

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: I would not spend another such a night

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: Though ’twere to buy a world of happy days,

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: So full of dismal terror was the time!

lines.speaker: KEEPER
lines.text: What was your dream, my lord? I pray you tell me.

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: Methoughts that I had broken from the Tower,

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: And was embarked to cross to Burgundy;

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: And in my company my brother Gloucester,

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: Who from my cabin tempted me to walk

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: Upon the hatches. Thence we looked toward England,

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: And cited up a thousand heavy times,

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: During the wars of York and Lancaster,

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: That had befall’n us. As we paced along

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: Upon the giddy footing of the hatches,

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: Methought that Gloucester stumbled, and in falling,

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: Struck me, that thought to stay him, overboard

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: Into the tumbling billows of the main.

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: O Lord, methought what pain it was to drown,

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: What dreadful noise of waters in my ears;

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: What sights of ugly death within my eyes.

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: Methoughts I saw a thousand fearful wracks;

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: A thousand men that fishes gnawed upon;

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: Wedges of gold, great anchors, heaps of pearl,

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: Inestimable stones, unvalued jewels,

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: All scattered in the bottom of the sea.

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: Some lay in dead men’s skulls, and in the holes

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: Where eyes did once inhabit there were crept—

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: As ’twere in scorn of eyes—reflecting gems,

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: That wooed the slimy bottom of the deep,

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: And mocked the dead bones that lay scattered by.

lines.speaker: KEEPER
lines.text: Had you such leisure in the time of death

lines.speaker: KEEPER
lines.text: To gaze upon these secrets of the deep?

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: Methought I had; and often did I strive

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: To yield the ghost, but still the envious flood

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: Stopped in my soul, and would not let it forth

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: To find the empty, vast, and wand’ring air,

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: But smothered it within my panting bulk,

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: Who almost burst to belch it in the sea.

lines.speaker: KEEPER
lines.text: Awaked you not in this sore agony?

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: No, no, my dream was lengthened after life.

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: O, then began the tempest to my soul.

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: I passed, methought, the melancholy flood,

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: With that sour ferryman which poets write of,

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: Unto the kingdom of perpetual night.

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: The first that there did greet my stranger-soul

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: Was my great father-in-law, renowned Warwick,

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: Who spake aloud, “What scourge for perjury

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: Can this dark monarchy afford false Clarence?”

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: And so he vanished. Then came wand’ring by

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: A shadow like an angel, with bright hair

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: Dabbled in blood; and he shrieked out aloud

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: “Clarence is come—false, fleeting, perjured Clarence,

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: That stabbed me in the field by Tewksbury!

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: Seize on him, Furies! Take him unto torment!”

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: With that, methoughts, a legion of foul fiends

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: Environed me, and howled in mine ears

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: Such hideous cries that with the very noise

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: I trembling waked, and for a season after

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: Could not believe but that I was in hell,

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: Such terrible impression made my dream.

lines.speaker: KEEPER
lines.text: No marvel, lord, though it affrighted you;

lines.speaker: KEEPER
lines.text: I am afraid, methinks, to hear you tell it.

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: Ah, Keeper, Keeper, I have done these things,

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: That now give evidence against my soul,

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: For Edward’s sake, and see how he requites me.

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: O God, if my deep prayers cannot appease Thee,

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: But Thou wilt be avenged on my misdeeds,

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: Yet execute Thy wrath in me alone;

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: O, spare my guiltless wife and my poor children!

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: Keeper, I prithee sit by me awhile.

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: My soul is heavy, and I fain would sleep.

lines.speaker: KEEPER
lines.text: I will, my lord; God give your Grace good rest.
[_Clarence reposes himself on a chair._]
Enter Brakenbury the Lieutenant.

lines.speaker: BRAKENBURY
lines.text: Sorrow breaks seasons and reposing hours,

lines.speaker: BRAKENBURY
lines.text: Makes the night morning, and the noontide night.

lines.speaker: BRAKENBURY
lines.text: Princes have but their titles for their glories,

lines.speaker: BRAKENBURY
lines.text: An outward honour for an inward toil;

lines.speaker: BRAKENBURY
lines.text: And, for unfelt imaginations,

lines.speaker: BRAKENBURY
lines.text: They often feel a world of restless cares,

lines.speaker: BRAKENBURY
lines.text: So that between their titles and low name,

lines.speaker: BRAKENBURY
lines.text: There’s nothing differs but the outward fame.
Enter the two Murderers.

lines.speaker: FIRST MURDERER
lines.text: Ho, who’s here?

lines.speaker: BRAKENBURY
lines.text: What wouldst thou, fellow? And how cam’st thou hither?

lines.speaker: SECOND MURDERER
lines.text: I would speak with Clarence, and I came hither on my legs.

lines.speaker: BRAKENBURY
lines.text: What, so brief?

lines.speaker: FIRST MURDERER
lines.text: ’Tis better, sir, than to be tedious. Let him see our commission, and

lines.speaker: FIRST MURDERER
lines.text: talk no more.
[_Brakenbury reads the commission._]

lines.speaker: BRAKENBURY
lines.text: I am in this commanded to deliver

lines.speaker: BRAKENBURY
lines.text: The noble Duke of Clarence to your hands.

lines.speaker: BRAKENBURY
lines.text: I will not reason what is meant hereby,

lines.speaker: BRAKENBURY
lines.text: Because I will be guiltless of the meaning.

lines.speaker: BRAKENBURY
lines.text: There lies the Duke asleep, and there the keys.

lines.speaker: BRAKENBURY
lines.text: I’ll to the King and signify to him

lines.speaker: BRAKENBURY
lines.text: That thus I have resigned to you my charge.

lines.speaker: FIRST MURDERER
lines.text: You may, sir; ’tis a point of wisdom. Fare you well.
[_Exeunt Brakenbury and the Keeper._]

lines.speaker: SECOND MURDERER
lines.text: What, shall I stab him as he sleeps?

lines.speaker: FIRST MURDERER
lines.text: No. He’ll say ’twas done cowardly, when he wakes.

lines.speaker: SECOND MURDERER
lines.text: Why, he shall never wake until the great Judgement Day.

lines.speaker: FIRST MURDERER
lines.text: Why, then he’ll say we stabbed him sleeping.

lines.speaker: SECOND MURDERER
lines.text: The urging of that word “judgement” hath bred a kind of remorse in me.

lines.speaker: FIRST MURDERER
lines.text: What, art thou afraid?

lines.speaker: SECOND MURDERER
lines.text: Not to kill him, having a warrant, but to be damned for killing him,

lines.speaker: SECOND MURDERER
lines.text: from the which no warrant can defend me.

lines.speaker: FIRST MURDERER
lines.text: I thought thou hadst been resolute.

lines.speaker: SECOND MURDERER
lines.text: So I am—to let him live.

lines.speaker: FIRST MURDERER
lines.text: I’ll back to the Duke of Gloucester and tell him so.

lines.speaker: SECOND MURDERER
lines.text: Nay, I prithee stay a little. I hope this passionate humour will

lines.speaker: SECOND MURDERER
lines.text: change. It was wont to hold me but while one tells twenty.

lines.speaker: FIRST MURDERER
lines.text: How dost thou feel thyself now?

lines.speaker: SECOND MURDERER
lines.text: Faith, some certain dregs of conscience are yet within me.

lines.speaker: FIRST MURDERER
lines.text: Remember our reward, when the deed’s done.

lines.speaker: SECOND MURDERER
lines.text: Zounds, he dies! I had forgot the reward.

lines.speaker: FIRST MURDERER
lines.text: Where’s thy conscience now?

lines.speaker: SECOND MURDERER
lines.text: O, in the Duke of Gloucester’s purse.

lines.speaker: FIRST MURDERER
lines.text: So, when he opens his purse to give us our reward, thy conscience flies

lines.speaker: FIRST MURDERER
lines.text: out.

lines.speaker: SECOND MURDERER
lines.text: ’Tis no matter; let it go. There’s few or none will entertain it.

lines.speaker: FIRST MURDERER
lines.text: What if it come to thee again?

lines.speaker: SECOND MURDERER
lines.text: I’ll not meddle with it; it makes a man coward. A man cannot steal but

lines.speaker: SECOND MURDERER
lines.text: it accuseth him; a man cannot swear but it checks him; a man cannot lie

lines.speaker: SECOND MURDERER
lines.text: with his neighbour’s wife but it detects him. ’Tis a blushing

lines.speaker: SECOND MURDERER
lines.text: shamefaced spirit that mutinies in a man’s bosom. It fills a man full

lines.speaker: SECOND MURDERER
lines.text: of obstacles. It made me once restore a purse of gold that by chance I

lines.speaker: SECOND MURDERER
lines.text: found. It beggars any man that keeps it. It is turned out of towns and

lines.speaker: SECOND MURDERER
lines.text: cities for a dangerous thing; and every man that means to live well

lines.speaker: SECOND MURDERER
lines.text: endeavours to trust to himself and live without it.

lines.speaker: FIRST MURDERER
lines.text: Zounds, ’tis even now at my elbow, persuading me not to kill the Duke.

lines.speaker: SECOND MURDERER
lines.text: Take the devil in thy mind, and believe him not. He would insinuate

lines.speaker: SECOND MURDERER
lines.text: with thee but to make thee sigh.

lines.speaker: FIRST MURDERER
lines.text: I am strong-framed; he cannot prevail with me.

lines.speaker: SECOND MURDERER
lines.text: Spoke like a tall man that respects thy reputation. Come, shall we fall

lines.speaker: SECOND MURDERER
lines.text: to work?

lines.speaker: FIRST MURDERER
lines.text: Take him on the costard with the hilts of thy sword, and then throw him

lines.speaker: FIRST MURDERER
lines.text: in the malmsey-butt in the next room.

lines.speaker: SECOND MURDERER
lines.text: O excellent device—and make a sop of him.

lines.speaker: FIRST MURDERER
lines.text: Soft, he wakes.

lines.speaker: SECOND MURDERER
lines.text: Strike!

lines.speaker: FIRST MURDERER
lines.text: No, we’ll reason with him.

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: Where art thou, keeper? Give me a cup of wine.

lines.speaker: SECOND MURDERER
lines.text: You shall have wine enough, my lord, anon.

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: In God’s name, what art thou?

lines.speaker: FIRST MURDERER
lines.text: A man, as you are.

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: But not as I am, royal.

lines.speaker: SECOND MURDERER
lines.text: Nor you as we are, loyal.

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: Thy voice is thunder, but thy looks are humble.

lines.speaker: FIRST MURDERER
lines.text: My voice is now the King’s, my looks mine own.

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: How darkly and how deadly dost thou speak!

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: Your eyes do menace me; why look you pale?

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: Who sent you hither? Wherefore do you come?

lines.speaker: SECOND MURDERER
lines.text: To, to, to—

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: To murder me?

lines.speaker: BOTH MURDERERS
lines.text: Ay, ay.

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: You scarcely have the hearts to tell me so,

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: And therefore cannot have the hearts to do it.

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: Wherein, my friends, have I offended you?

lines.speaker: FIRST MURDERER
lines.text: Offended us you have not, but the King.

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: I shall be reconciled to him again.

lines.speaker: SECOND MURDERER
lines.text: Never, my lord; therefore prepare to die.

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: Are you drawn forth among a world of men

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: To slay the innocent? What is my offence?

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: Where is the evidence that doth accuse me?

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: What lawful quest have given their verdict up

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: Unto the frowning judge? Or who pronounced

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: The bitter sentence of poor Clarence’ death?

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: Before I be convict by course of law,

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: To threaten me with death is most unlawful.

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: I charge you, as you hope to have redemption,

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: By Christ’s dear blood shed for our grievous sins,

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: That you depart, and lay no hands on me.

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: The deed you undertake is damnable.

lines.speaker: FIRST MURDERER
lines.text: What we will do, we do upon command.

lines.speaker: SECOND MURDERER
lines.text: And he that hath commanded is our King.

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: Erroneous vassals! The great King of kings

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: Hath in the table of his law commanded

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: That thou shalt do no murder. Will you then

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: Spurn at His edict and fulfil a man’s?

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: Take heed, for He holds vengeance in His hand

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: To hurl upon their heads that break His law.

lines.speaker: SECOND MURDERER
lines.text: And that same vengeance doth He hurl on thee

lines.speaker: SECOND MURDERER
lines.text: For false forswearing, and for murder too.

lines.speaker: SECOND MURDERER
lines.text: Thou didst receive the sacrament to fight

lines.speaker: SECOND MURDERER
lines.text: In quarrel of the house of Lancaster.

lines.speaker: FIRST MURDERER
lines.text: And like a traitor to the name of God

lines.speaker: FIRST MURDERER
lines.text: Didst break that vow, and with thy treacherous blade

lines.speaker: FIRST MURDERER
lines.text: Unrippedst the bowels of thy sovereign’s son.

lines.speaker: SECOND MURDERER
lines.text: Whom thou wast sworn to cherish and defend.

lines.speaker: FIRST MURDERER
lines.text: How canst thou urge God’s dreadful law to us,

lines.speaker: FIRST MURDERER
lines.text: When thou hast broke it in such dear degree?

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: Alas, for whose sake did I that ill deed?

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: For Edward, for my brother, for his sake.

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: He sends you not to murder me for this,

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: For in that sin he is as deep as I.

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: If God will be avenged for the deed,

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: O, know you yet He doth it publicly;

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: Take not the quarrel from His powerful arm;

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: He needs no indirect or lawless course

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: To cut off those that have offended Him.

lines.speaker: FIRST MURDERER
lines.text: Who made thee then a bloody minister

lines.speaker: FIRST MURDERER
lines.text: When gallant-springing, brave Plantagenet,

lines.speaker: FIRST MURDERER
lines.text: That princely novice, was struck dead by thee?

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: My brother’s love, the devil, and my rage.

lines.speaker: FIRST MURDERER
lines.text: Thy brother’s love, our duty, and thy faults,

lines.speaker: FIRST MURDERER
lines.text: Provoke us hither now to slaughter thee.

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: If you do love my brother, hate not me.

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: I am his brother, and I love him well.

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: If you are hired for meed, go back again,

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: And I will send you to my brother Gloucester,

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: Who shall reward you better for my life

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: Than Edward will for tidings of my death.

lines.speaker: SECOND MURDERER
lines.text: You are deceived. Your brother Gloucester hates you.

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: O no, he loves me, and he holds me dear.

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: Go you to him from me.

lines.speaker: FIRST MURDERER
lines.text: Ay, so we will.

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: Tell him when that our princely father York

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: Blessed his three sons with his victorious arm,

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: And charged us from his soul to love each other,

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: He little thought of this divided friendship.

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: Bid Gloucester think of this, and he will weep.

lines.speaker: FIRST MURDERER
lines.text: Ay, millstones, as he lessoned us to weep.

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: O, do not slander him, for he is kind.

lines.speaker: FIRST MURDERER
lines.text: Right, as snow in harvest. Come, you deceive yourself.

lines.speaker: FIRST MURDERER
lines.text: ’Tis he that sends us to destroy you here.

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: It cannot be, for he bewept my fortune,

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: And hugged me in his arms, and swore with sobs

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: That he would labour my delivery.

lines.speaker: FIRST MURDERER
lines.text: Why, so he doth, when he delivers you

lines.speaker: FIRST MURDERER
lines.text: From this earth’s thraldom to the joys of heaven.

lines.speaker: SECOND MURDERER
lines.text: Make peace with God, for you must die, my lord.

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: Have you that holy feeling in your souls

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: To counsel me to make my peace with God,

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: And are you yet to your own souls so blind

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: That you will war with God by murd’ring me?

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: O sirs, consider: they that set you on

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: To do this deed will hate you for the deed.

lines.speaker: SECOND MURDERER
lines.text: What shall we do?

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: Relent, and save your souls.

lines.speaker: FIRST MURDERER
lines.text: Relent? No, ’tis cowardly and womanish.

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: Not to relent is beastly, savage, devilish.

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: Which of you—if you were a prince’s son,

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: Being pent from liberty, as I am now—

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: If two such murderers as yourselves came to you,

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: Would not entreat for life? Ay, you would beg,

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: Were you in my distress.

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: My friend, I spy some pity in thy looks.

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: O, if thine eye be not a flatterer,

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: Come thou on my side, and entreat for me;

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: A begging prince what beggar pities not?

lines.speaker: SECOND MURDERER
lines.text: Look behind you, my lord.

lines.speaker: FIRST MURDERER
lines.text: Take that, and that! [_Stabs him._] If all this will not do,

lines.speaker: FIRST MURDERER
lines.text: I’ll drown you in the malmsey-butt within.
[_Exit with the body._]

lines.speaker: SECOND MURDERER
lines.text: A bloody deed, and desperately dispatched.

lines.speaker: SECOND MURDERER
lines.text: How fain, like Pilate, would I wash my hands

lines.speaker: SECOND MURDERER
lines.text: Of this most grievous murder.
Enter First Murderer.

lines.speaker: FIRST MURDERER
lines.text: How now? What mean’st thou that thou help’st me not?

lines.speaker: FIRST MURDERER
lines.text: By heavens, the Duke shall know how slack you have been.

lines.speaker: SECOND MURDERER
lines.text: I would he knew that I had saved his brother.

lines.speaker: SECOND MURDERER
lines.text: Take thou the fee, and tell him what I say,

lines.speaker: SECOND MURDERER
lines.text: For I repent me that the Duke is slain.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: FIRST MURDERER
lines.text: So do not I. Go, coward as thou art.

lines.speaker: FIRST MURDERER
lines.text: Well, I’ll go hide the body in some hole

lines.speaker: FIRST MURDERER
lines.text: Till that the Duke give order for his burial.

lines.speaker: FIRST MURDERER
lines.text: And when I have my meed, I will away,

lines.speaker: FIRST MURDERER
lines.text: For this will out, and then I must not stay.
[_Exit._]

scenes.setting: London. A Room in the palace

lines.text: Enter King Edward, sick, Queen Elizabeth, Dorset, Rivers, Hastings, Buckingham, Grey and others.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Why, so. Now have I done a good day’s work.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: You peers, continue this united league.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: I every day expect an embassage

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: From my Redeemer, to redeem me hence;

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: And more at peace my soul shall part to heaven

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Since I have made my friends at peace on earth.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Rivers and Hastings, take each other’s hand;

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Dissemble not your hatred. Swear your love.

lines.speaker: RIVERS
lines.text: By heaven, my soul is purged from grudging hate,

lines.speaker: RIVERS
lines.text: And with my hand I seal my true heart’s love.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: So thrive I, as I truly swear the like.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Take heed you dally not before your King,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Lest He that is the supreme King of kings

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Confound your hidden falsehood, and award

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Either of you to be the other’s end.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: So prosper I, as I swear perfect love.

lines.speaker: RIVERS
lines.text: And I, as I love Hastings with my heart.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Madam, yourself is not exempt from this;

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Nor you, son Dorset; Buckingham, nor you.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: You have been factious one against the other.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Wife, love Lord Hastings, let him kiss your hand,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: And what you do, do it unfeignedly.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: There, Hastings, I will never more remember

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Our former hatred, so thrive I and mine.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Dorset, embrace him; Hastings, love lord Marquess.

lines.speaker: DORSET
lines.text: This interchange of love, I here protest,

lines.speaker: DORSET
lines.text: Upon my part shall be inviolable.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: And so swear I.
[_They embrace._]

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Now, princely Buckingham, seal thou this league

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: With thy embracements to my wife’s allies,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: And make me happy in your unity.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Whenever Buckingham doth turn his hate

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Upon your Grace, but with all duteous love

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Doth cherish you and yours, God punish me

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: With hate in those where I expect most love.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: When I have most need to employ a friend,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: And most assured that he is a friend,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Deep, hollow, treacherous, and full of guile

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Be he unto me: this do I beg of God,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: When I am cold in love to you or yours.
[_Embrace._]

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: A pleasing cordial, princely Buckingham,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Is this thy vow unto my sickly heart.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: There wanteth now our brother Gloucester here,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: To make the blessed period of this peace.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: And in good time,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Here comes Sir Ratcliffe and the Duke.
Enter Ratcliffe and Richard.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Good morrow to my sovereign King and Queen;

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And, princely peers, a happy time of day.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Happy indeed, as we have spent the day.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Gloucester, we have done deeds of charity,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Made peace of enmity, fair love of hate,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Between these swelling wrong-incensed peers.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: A blessed labour, my most sovereign lord,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Among this princely heap, if any here

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: By false intelligence or wrong surmise

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Hold me a foe,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: If I unwittingly, or in my rage,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Have aught committed that is hardly borne

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: By any in this presence, I desire

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: To reconcile me to his friendly peace.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: ’Tis death to me to be at enmity;

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: I hate it, and desire all good men’s love.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: First, madam, I entreat true peace of you,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Which I will purchase with my duteous service;

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Of you, my noble cousin Buckingham,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: If ever any grudge were lodged between us;

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Of you and you, Lord Rivers and of Dorset,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: That all without desert have frowned on me;

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Of you, Lord Woodville and Lord Scales;—of you,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Dukes, earls, lords, gentlemen; indeed, of all.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: I do not know that Englishman alive

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: With whom my soul is any jot at odds

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: More than the infant that is born tonight.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: I thank my God for my humility.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: A holy day shall this be kept hereafter.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: I would to God all strifes were well compounded.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: My sovereign lord, I do beseech your Highness

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: To take our brother Clarence to your grace.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Why, madam, have I offered love for this,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: To be so flouted in this royal presence?

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Who knows not that the gentle Duke is dead?
[_They all start._]

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: You do him injury to scorn his corse.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Who knows not he is dead! Who knows he is?

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: All-seeing heaven, what a world is this!

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Look I so pale, Lord Dorset, as the rest?

lines.speaker: DORSET
lines.text: Ay, my good lord, and no man in the presence

lines.speaker: DORSET
lines.text: But his red colour hath forsook his cheeks.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Is Clarence dead? The order was reversed.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: But he, poor man, by your first order died,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And that a winged Mercury did bear;

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Some tardy cripple bore the countermand,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: That came too lag to see him buried.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: God grant that some, less noble and less loyal,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Nearer in bloody thoughts, and not in blood,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Deserve not worse than wretched Clarence did,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And yet go current from suspicion!
Enter Stanley Earl of Derby.

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: A boon, my sovereign, for my service done!

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: I prithee, peace. My soul is full of sorrow.

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: I will not rise unless your Highness hear me.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Then say at once what is it thou requests.

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: The forfeit, sovereign, of my servant’s life

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: Who slew today a riotous gentleman

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: Lately attendant on the Duke of Norfolk.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Have I a tongue to doom my brother’s death,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: And shall that tongue give pardon to a slave?

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: My brother killed no man; his fault was thought,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: And yet his punishment was bitter death.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Who sued to me for him? Who, in my wrath,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Kneeled at my feet, and bid me be advised?

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Who spoke of brotherhood? Who spoke of love?

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Who told me how the poor soul did forsake

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: The mighty Warwick, and did fight for me?

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Who told me, in the field at Tewksbury,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: When Oxford had me down, he rescued me,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: And said, “Dear brother, live, and be a king”?

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Who told me, when we both lay in the field

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Frozen almost to death, how he did lap me

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Even in his garments, and did give himself,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: All thin and naked, to the numb-cold night?

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: All this from my remembrance brutish wrath

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Sinfully plucked, and not a man of you

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Had so much grace to put it in my mind.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: But when your carters or your waiting vassals

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Have done a drunken slaughter, and defaced

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: The precious image of our dear Redeemer,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: You straight are on your knees for pardon, pardon,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: And I, unjustly too, must grant it you.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: But for my brother not a man would speak,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Nor I, ungracious, speak unto myself

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: For him, poor soul. The proudest of you all

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Have been beholding to him in his life,

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Yet none of you would once beg for his life.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: O God, I fear Thy justice will take hold

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: On me, and you, and mine and yours for this!

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Come, Hastings, help me to my closet.

lines.speaker: KING EDWARD
lines.text: Ah, poor Clarence!
[_Exeunt some with King and Queen._]

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: This is the fruit of rashness. Marked you not

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: How that the guilty kindred of the Queen

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Looked pale when they did hear of Clarence’ death?

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: O, they did urge it still unto the King.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: God will revenge it. Come, lords, will you go

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: To comfort Edward with our company?

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: We wait upon your Grace.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter the old Duchess of York with the two Children of Clarence.

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: Good grandam, tell us, is our father dead?

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: No, boy.

lines.speaker: GIRL
lines.text: Why do you weep so oft, and beat your breast,

lines.speaker: GIRL
lines.text: And cry “O Clarence, my unhappy son”?

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: Why do you look on us, and shake your head,

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: And call us orphans, wretches, castaways,

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: If that our noble father were alive?

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: My pretty cousins, you mistake me both.

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: I do lament the sickness of the King,

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: As loath to lose him, not your father’s death.

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: It were lost sorrow to wail one that’s lost.

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: Then you conclude, my grandam, he is dead.

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: The King mine uncle is to blame for it.

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: God will revenge it, whom I will importune

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: With earnest prayers all to that effect.

lines.speaker: GIRL
lines.text: And so will I.

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: Peace, children, peace. The King doth love you well.

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: Incapable and shallow innocents,

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: You cannot guess who caused your father’s death.

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: Grandam, we can, for my good uncle Gloucester

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: Told me, the King, provoked to it by the Queen,

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: Devised impeachments to imprison him;

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: And when my uncle told me so, he wept,

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: And pitied me, and kindly kissed my cheek;

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: Bade me rely on him as on my father,

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: And he would love me dearly as his child.

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: Ah, that deceit should steal such gentle shape,

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: And with a virtuous visard hide deep vice!

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: He is my son, ay, and therein my shame;

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: Yet from my dugs he drew not this deceit.

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: Think you my uncle did dissemble, grandam?

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: Ay, boy.

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: I cannot think it. Hark, what noise is this?
Enter Queen Elizabeth with her hair about her ears, Rivers and Dorset after her.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Ah, who shall hinder me to wail and weep,

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: To chide my fortune, and torment myself?

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: I’ll join with black despair against my soul

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: And to myself become an enemy.

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: What means this scene of rude impatience?

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: To make an act of tragic violence.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Edward, my lord, thy son, our King, is dead.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Why grow the branches when the root is gone?

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Why wither not the leaves that want their sap?

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: If you will live, lament; if die, be brief,

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: That our swift-winged souls may catch the King’s

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Or, like obedient subjects, follow him

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: To his new kingdom of ne’er-changing night.

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: Ah, so much interest have I in thy sorrow

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: As I had title in thy noble husband.

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: I have bewept a worthy husband’s death,

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: And lived by looking on his images;

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: But now two mirrors of his princely semblance

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: Are cracked in pieces by malignant death,

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: And I, for comfort, have but one false glass,

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: That grieves me when I see my shame in him.

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: Thou art a widow, yet thou art a mother,

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: And hast the comfort of thy children left;

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: But death hath snatched my husband from mine arms

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: And plucked two crutches from my feeble hands,

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: Clarence and Edward. O, what cause have I,

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: Thine being but a moiety of my moan,

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: To overgo thy woes and drown thy cries.

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: Ah, aunt, you wept not for our father’s death.

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: How can we aid you with our kindred tears?

lines.speaker: GIRL
lines.text: Our fatherless distress was left unmoaned.

lines.speaker: GIRL
lines.text: Your widow-dolour likewise be unwept!

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Give me no help in lamentation.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: I am not barren to bring forth complaints.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: All springs reduce their currents to mine eyes,

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: That I, being governed by the watery moon,

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: May send forth plenteous tears to drown the world.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Ah, for my husband, for my dear Lord Edward!

lines.speaker: CHILDREN
lines.text: Ah for our father, for our dear Lord Clarence!

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: Alas for both, both mine, Edward and Clarence!

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: What stay had I but Edward? And he’s gone.

lines.speaker: CHILDREN
lines.text: What stay had we but Clarence? And he’s gone.

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: What stays had I but they? And they are gone.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Was never widow had so dear a loss.

lines.speaker: CHILDREN
lines.text: Were never orphans had so dear a loss.

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: Was never mother had so dear a loss.

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: Alas, I am the mother of these griefs.

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: Their woes are parcelled, mine is general.

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: She for an Edward weeps, and so do I;

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: I for a Clarence weep, so doth not she;

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: These babes for Clarence weep, and so do I;

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: I for an Edward weep, so do not they.

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: Alas, you three, on me, threefold distressed,

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: Pour all your tears. I am your sorrow’s nurse,

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: And I will pamper it with lamentation.

lines.speaker: DORSET
lines.text: Comfort, dear mother. God is much displeased

lines.speaker: DORSET
lines.text: That you take with unthankfulness His doing.

lines.speaker: DORSET
lines.text: In common worldly things ’tis called ungrateful

lines.speaker: DORSET
lines.text: With dull unwillingness to repay a debt

lines.speaker: DORSET
lines.text: Which with a bounteous hand was kindly lent;

lines.speaker: DORSET
lines.text: Much more to be thus opposite with heaven,

lines.speaker: DORSET
lines.text: For it requires the royal debt it lent you.

lines.speaker: RIVERS
lines.text: Madam, bethink you, like a careful mother,

lines.speaker: RIVERS
lines.text: Of the young prince your son. Send straight for him;

lines.speaker: RIVERS
lines.text: Let him be crowned; in him your comfort lives.

lines.speaker: RIVERS
lines.text: Drown desperate sorrow in dead Edward’s grave,

lines.speaker: RIVERS
lines.text: And plant your joys in living Edward’s throne.
Enter Richard, Buckingham, Stanley Earl of Derby, Hastings and Ratcliffe.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Sister, have comfort. All of us have cause

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: To wail the dimming of our shining star,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: But none can help our harms by wailing them.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Madam my mother, I do cry you mercy;

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: I did not see your Grace. Humbly on my knee

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: I crave your blessing.
[_Kneels._]

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: God bless thee, and put meekness in thy breast,

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: Love, charity, obedience, and true duty.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Amen. [_Aside_.] And make me die a good old man!

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: That is the butt end of a mother’s blessing;

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: I marvel that her Grace did leave it out.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: You cloudy princes and heart-sorrowing peers

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: That bear this heavy mutual load of moan,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Now cheer each other in each other’s love.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Though we have spent our harvest of this king,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: We are to reap the harvest of his son.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: The broken rancour of your high-swoll’n hates,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: But lately splintered, knit, and joined together,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Must gently be preserved, cherished, and kept.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Me seemeth good that with some little train,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Forthwith from Ludlow the young Prince be fet

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Hither to London, to be crowned our King.

lines.speaker: RIVERS
lines.text: Why with some little train, my Lord of Buckingham?

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Marry, my lord, lest by a multitude

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: The new-healed wound of malice should break out,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Which would be so much the more dangerous

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: By how much the estate is green and yet ungoverned.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Where every horse bears his commanding rein

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: And may direct his course as please himself,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: As well the fear of harm as harm apparent,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: In my opinion, ought to be prevented.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: I hope the King made peace with all of us;

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And the compact is firm and true in me.

lines.speaker: RIVERS
lines.text: And so in me, and so, I think, in all.

lines.speaker: RIVERS
lines.text: Yet since it is but green, it should be put

lines.speaker: RIVERS
lines.text: To no apparent likelihood of breach,

lines.speaker: RIVERS
lines.text: Which haply by much company might be urged.

lines.speaker: RIVERS
lines.text: Therefore I say with noble Buckingham

lines.speaker: RIVERS
lines.text: That it is meet so few should fetch the Prince.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: And so say I.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Then be it so, and go we to determine

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Who they shall be that straight shall post to Ludlow.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Madam, and you, my sister, will you go

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: To give your censures in this business?
[_Exeunt all but Buckingham and Richard._]

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: My lord, whoever journeys to the Prince,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: For God’s sake, let not us two stay at home.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: For by the way I’ll sort occasion,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: As index to the story we late talked of,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: To part the Queen’s proud kindred from the Prince.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: My other self, my counsel’s consistory,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: My oracle, my prophet, my dear cousin,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: I, as a child, will go by thy direction.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Toward Ludlow then, for we’ll not stay behind.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter one Citizen at one door, and Another at the other.

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: Good morrow, neighbour, whither away so fast?

lines.speaker: SECOND CITIZEN
lines.text: I promise you, I scarcely know myself.

lines.speaker: SECOND CITIZEN
lines.text: Hear you the news abroad?

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: Yes, that the King is dead.

lines.speaker: SECOND CITIZEN
lines.text: Ill news, by’r Lady; seldom comes the better.

lines.speaker: SECOND CITIZEN
lines.text: I fear, I fear ’twill prove a giddy world.
Enter another Citizen.

lines.speaker: THIRD CITIZEN
lines.text: Neighbours, God speed.

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: Give you good morrow, sir.

lines.speaker: THIRD CITIZEN
lines.text: Doth the news hold of good King Edward’s death?

lines.speaker: SECOND CITIZEN
lines.text: Ay, sir, it is too true, God help the while.

lines.speaker: THIRD CITIZEN
lines.text: Then, masters, look to see a troublous world.

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: No, no; by God’s good grace, his son shall reign.

lines.speaker: THIRD CITIZEN
lines.text: Woe to that land that’s governed by a child.

lines.speaker: SECOND CITIZEN
lines.text: In him there is a hope of government,

lines.speaker: SECOND CITIZEN
