lines.text: Which, in his nonage, council under him,

lines.speaker: SECOND CITIZEN
lines.text: And, in his full and ripened years, himself,

lines.speaker: SECOND CITIZEN
lines.text: No doubt shall then, and till then, govern well.

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: So stood the state when Henry the Sixth

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: Was crowned in Paris but at nine months old.

lines.speaker: THIRD CITIZEN
lines.text: Stood the state so? No, no, good friends, God wot.

lines.speaker: THIRD CITIZEN
lines.text: For then this land was famously enriched

lines.speaker: THIRD CITIZEN
lines.text: With politic grave counsel; then the King

lines.speaker: THIRD CITIZEN
lines.text: Had virtuous uncles to protect his Grace.

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: Why, so hath this, both by his father and mother.

lines.speaker: THIRD CITIZEN
lines.text: Better it were they all came by his father,

lines.speaker: THIRD CITIZEN
lines.text: Or by his father there were none at all,

lines.speaker: THIRD CITIZEN
lines.text: For emulation who shall now be nearest

lines.speaker: THIRD CITIZEN
lines.text: Will touch us all too near, if God prevent not.

lines.speaker: THIRD CITIZEN
lines.text: O, full of danger is the Duke of Gloucester,

lines.speaker: THIRD CITIZEN
lines.text: And the Queen’s sons and brothers haught and proud;

lines.speaker: THIRD CITIZEN
lines.text: And were they to be ruled, and not to rule,

lines.speaker: THIRD CITIZEN
lines.text: This sickly land might solace as before.

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: Come, come, we fear the worst; all will be well.

lines.speaker: THIRD CITIZEN
lines.text: When clouds are seen, wise men put on their cloaks;

lines.speaker: THIRD CITIZEN
lines.text: When great leaves fall, then winter is at hand;

lines.speaker: THIRD CITIZEN
lines.text: When the sun sets, who doth not look for night?

lines.speaker: THIRD CITIZEN
lines.text: Untimely storms make men expect a dearth.

lines.speaker: THIRD CITIZEN
lines.text: All may be well; but, if God sort it so,

lines.speaker: THIRD CITIZEN
lines.text: ’Tis more than we deserve or I expect.

lines.speaker: SECOND CITIZEN
lines.text: Truly, the hearts of men are full of fear.

lines.speaker: SECOND CITIZEN
lines.text: You cannot reason almost with a man

lines.speaker: SECOND CITIZEN
lines.text: That looks not heavily and full of dread.

lines.speaker: THIRD CITIZEN
lines.text: Before the days of change, still is it so.

lines.speaker: THIRD CITIZEN
lines.text: By a divine instinct men’s minds mistrust

lines.speaker: THIRD CITIZEN
lines.text: Ensuing danger, as by proof we see

lines.speaker: THIRD CITIZEN
lines.text: The water swell before a boist’rous storm.

lines.speaker: THIRD CITIZEN
lines.text: But leave it all to God. Whither away?

lines.speaker: SECOND CITIZEN
lines.text: Marry, we were sent for to the Justices.

lines.speaker: THIRD CITIZEN
lines.text: And so was I. I’ll bear you company.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: London. A Room in the Palace

lines.text: Enter the Archbishop of York, the young Duke of York, Queen Elizabeth and the Duchess of York.

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: Last night, I hear, they lay at Stony Stratford,

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: And at Northampton they do rest tonight.

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: Tomorrow or next day they will be here.

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: I long with all my heart to see the Prince.

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: I hope he is much grown since last I saw him.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: But I hear no; they say my son of York

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Has almost overta’en him in his growth.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Ay, mother, but I would not have it so.

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: Why, my good cousin? It is good to grow.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Grandam, one night as we did sit at supper,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: My uncle Rivers talked how I did grow

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: More than my brother. “Ay,” quoth my uncle Gloucester,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: “Small herbs have grace; great weeds do grow apace.”

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: And since, methinks I would not grow so fast,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Because sweet flowers are slow and weeds make haste.

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: Good faith, good faith, the saying did not hold

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: In him that did object the same to thee!

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: He was the wretched’st thing when he was young,

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: So long a-growing and so leisurely,

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: That if his rule were true, he should be gracious.

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: And so no doubt he is, my gracious madam.

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: I hope he is, but yet let mothers doubt.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Now, by my troth, if I had been remembered,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: I could have given my uncle’s Grace a flout

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: To touch his growth nearer than he touched mine.

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: How, my young York? I prithee let me hear it.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Marry, they say my uncle grew so fast

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: That he could gnaw a crust at two hours old.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: ’Twas full two years ere I could get a tooth.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Grandam, this would have been a biting jest.

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: I prithee, pretty York, who told thee this?

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Grandam, his nurse.

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: His nurse? Why she was dead ere thou wast born.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: If ’twere not she, I cannot tell who told me.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: A parlous boy! Go to, you are too shrewd.

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: Good madam, be not angry with the child.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Pitchers have ears.
Enter a Messenger.

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: Here comes a messenger. What news?

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Such news, my lord, as grieves me to report.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: How doth the Prince?

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Well, madam, and in health.

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: What is thy news?

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Lord Rivers and Lord Grey are sent to Pomfret,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: And, with them Sir Thomas Vaughan, prisoners.

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: Who hath committed them?

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: The mighty Dukes, Gloucester and Buckingham.

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: For what offence?

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: The sum of all I can, I have disclosed.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Why or for what the nobles were committed

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Is all unknown to me, my gracious lord.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Ah me! I see the ruin of my house.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: The tiger now hath seized the gentle hind;

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Insulting tyranny begins to jut

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Upon the innocent and aweless throne.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Welcome, destruction, blood, and massacre;

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: I see, as in a map, the end of all.

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: Accursed and unquiet wrangling days,

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: How many of you have mine eyes beheld?

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: My husband lost his life to get the crown,

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: And often up and down my sons were tossed

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: For me to joy and weep their gain and loss.

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: And being seated, and domestic broils

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: Clean over-blown, themselves, the conquerors

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: Make war upon themselves, brother to brother,

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: Blood to blood, self against self. O, preposterous

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: And frantic outrage, end thy damned spleen,

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: Or let me die, to look on earth no more.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Come, come, my boy. We will to sanctuary.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Madam, farewell.

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: Stay, I will go with you.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: You have no cause.
[_To the Queen._]

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: My gracious lady, go,

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: And thither bear your treasure and your goods.

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: For my part, I’ll resign unto your Grace

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: The seal I keep; and so betide to me

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: As well I tender you and all of yours.

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: Go, I’ll conduct you to the sanctuary.
[_Exeunt._]
The trumpets sound. Enter young Prince Edward, Richard, Buckingham, Cardinal Bourchier, Catesby and others.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Welcome, sweet Prince, to London, to your chamber.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Welcome, dear cousin, my thoughts’ sovereign.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: The weary way hath made you melancholy.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: No, uncle, but our crosses on the way

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Have made it tedious, wearisome, and heavy.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: I want more uncles here to welcome me.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Sweet prince, the untainted virtue of your years

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Hath not yet dived into the world’s deceit,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Nor more can you distinguish of a man

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Than of his outward show, which, God He knows,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Seldom or never jumpeth with the heart.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Those uncles which you want were dangerous;

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Your Grace attended to their sugared words

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: But looked not on the poison of their hearts.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: God keep you from them, and from such false friends!

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: God keep me from false friends, but they were none.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: My lord, the Mayor of London comes to greet you.
Enter Lord Mayor with Attendants.

lines.speaker: MAYOR
lines.text: God bless your Grace with health and happy days!

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: I thank you, good my lord, and thank you all.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: I thought my mother and my brother York

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Would long ere this have met us on the way.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Fie, what a slug is Hastings, that he comes not

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: To tell us whether they will come or no!
Enter Lord Hastings.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: And in good time, here comes the sweating lord.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Welcome, my lord. What, will our mother come?

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: On what occasion God He knows, not I,

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: The Queen your mother and your brother York

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: Have taken sanctuary. The tender prince

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: Would fain have come with me to meet your Grace,

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: But by his mother was perforce withheld.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Fie, what an indirect and peevish course

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Is this of hers? Lord cardinal, will your Grace

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Persuade the Queen to send the Duke of York

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Unto his princely brother presently?

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: If she deny, Lord Hastings, go with him,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: And from her jealous arms pluck him perforce.

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: My Lord of Buckingham, if my weak oratory

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: Can from his mother win the Duke of York,

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: Anon expect him here; but if she be obdurate

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: To mild entreaties, God in heaven forbid

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: We should infringe the holy privilege

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: Of blessed sanctuary! Not for all this land

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: Would I be guilty of so deep a sin.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: You are too senseless-obstinate, my lord,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Too ceremonious and traditional.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Weigh it but with the grossness of this age,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: You break not sanctuary in seizing him.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: The benefit thereof is always granted

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: To those whose dealings have deserved the place

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: And those who have the wit to claim the place.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: This prince hath neither claimed it nor deserved it

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: And therefore, in mine opinion, cannot have it.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Then taking him from thence that is not there,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: You break no privilege nor charter there.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Oft have I heard of sanctuary-men,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: But sanctuary children, never till now.

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: My lord, you shall o’errule my mind for once.

lines.speaker: CARDINAL
lines.text: Come on, Lord Hastings, will you go with me?

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: I go, my lord.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Good lords, make all the speedy haste you may.
[_Exeunt Cardinal and Hastings._]

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Say, uncle Gloucester, if our brother come,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Where shall we sojourn till our coronation?

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Where it seems best unto your royal self.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: If I may counsel you, some day or two

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Your Highness shall repose you at the Tower,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Then where you please and shall be thought most fit

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: For your best health and recreation.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: I do not like the Tower, of any place.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Did Julius Caesar build that place, my lord?

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: He did, my gracious lord, begin that place,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Which, since, succeeding ages have re-edified.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Is it upon record, or else reported

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Successively from age to age, he built it?

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Upon record, my gracious lord.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: But say, my lord, it were not registered,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Methinks the truth should live from age to age,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: As ’twere retailed to all posterity,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Even to the general all-ending day.
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: So wise so young, they say, do never live long.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: What say you, uncle?

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: I say, without characters, fame lives long.
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Thus, like the formal Vice, Iniquity,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: I moralize two meanings in one word.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: That Julius Caesar was a famous man.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: With what his valour did enrich his wit,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: His wit set down to make his valour live;

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Death makes no conquest of this conqueror,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: For now he lives in fame, though not in life.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: I’ll tell you what, my cousin Buckingham.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: What, my gracious lord?

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: An if I live until I be a man,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: I’ll win our ancient right in France again,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Or die a soldier, as I lived a king.
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Short summers lightly have a forward spring.
Enter young Duke of York, Hastings and the Cardinal.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Now, in good time here comes the Duke of York.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Richard of York, how fares our loving brother?

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Well, my dread lord—so must I call you now.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Ay brother, to our grief, as it is yours.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Too late he died that might have kept that title,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Which by his death hath lost much majesty.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: How fares our cousin, noble lord of York?

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: I thank you, gentle uncle. O, my lord,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: You said that idle weeds are fast in growth.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: The Prince my brother hath outgrown me far.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: He hath, my lord.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: And therefore is he idle?

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: O, my fair cousin, I must not say so.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Then he is more beholding to you than I.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: He may command me as my sovereign,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: But you have power in me as in a kinsman.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: I pray you, uncle, give me this dagger.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: My dagger, little cousin? With all my heart.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: A beggar, brother?

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Of my kind uncle, that I know will give,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: And being but a toy, which is no grief to give.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: A greater gift than that I’ll give my cousin.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: A greater gift? O, that’s the sword to it.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Ay, gentle cousin, were it light enough.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: O, then I see you will part but with light gifts;

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: In weightier things you’ll say a beggar nay.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: It is too heavy for your Grace to wear.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: I weigh it lightly, were it heavier.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: What, would you have my weapon, little lord?

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: I would, that I might thank you as you call me.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: How?

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Little.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: My lord of York will still be cross in talk.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Uncle, your Grace knows how to bear with him.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: You mean, to bear me, not to bear with me.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Uncle, my brother mocks both you and me.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Because that I am little, like an ape,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: He thinks that you should bear me on your shoulders.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: With what a sharp-provided wit he reasons!

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: To mitigate the scorn he gives his uncle,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: He prettily and aptly taunts himself.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: So cunning and so young is wonderful.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: My lord, wil’t please you pass along?

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Myself and my good cousin Buckingham

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Will to your mother, to entreat of her

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: To meet you at the Tower and welcome you.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: What, will you go unto the Tower, my lord?

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: My Lord Protector needs will have it so.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: I shall not sleep in quiet at the Tower.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Why, what should you fear?

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Marry, my uncle Clarence’ angry ghost.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: My grandam told me he was murdered there.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: I fear no uncles dead.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Nor none that live, I hope.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: An if they live, I hope I need not fear.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: But come, my lord. With a heavy heart,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Thinking on them, go I unto the Tower.
[_A Sennet. Exeunt Prince Edward, York, Hastings, Dorset and all but Richard, Buckingham and Catesby._]

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Think you, my lord, this little prating York

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Was not incensed by his subtle mother

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: To taunt and scorn you thus opprobriously?

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: No doubt, no doubt. O, ’tis a parlous boy,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Bold, quick, ingenious, forward, capable.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: He is all the mother’s, from the top to toe.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Well, let them rest. Come hither, Catesby.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Thou art sworn as deeply to effect what we intend

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: As closely to conceal what we impart.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Thou know’st our reasons urged upon the way.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: What think’st thou? Is it not an easy matter

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: To make William Lord Hastings of our mind

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: For the instalment of this noble Duke

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: In the seat royal of this famous isle?

lines.speaker: CATESBY
lines.text: He for his father’s sake so loves the Prince

lines.speaker: CATESBY
lines.text: That he will not be won to aught against him.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: What think’st thou then of Stanley? Will not he?

lines.speaker: CATESBY
lines.text: He will do all in all as Hastings doth.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Well then, no more but this: go, gentle Catesby,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: And, as it were far off, sound thou Lord Hastings

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: How he doth stand affected to our purpose,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: And summon him tomorrow to the Tower

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: To sit about the coronation.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: If thou dost find him tractable to us,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Encourage him, and tell him all our reasons.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: If he be leaden, icy, cold, unwilling,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Be thou so too, and so break off the talk,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: And give us notice of his inclination;

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: For we tomorrow hold divided councils,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Wherein thyself shalt highly be employed.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Commend me to Lord William. Tell him, Catesby,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: His ancient knot of dangerous adversaries

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Tomorrow are let blood at Pomfret Castle,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And bid my lord, for joy of this good news,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Give Mistress Shore one gentle kiss the more.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Good Catesby, go effect this business soundly.

lines.speaker: CATESBY
lines.text: My good lords both, with all the heed I can.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Shall we hear from you, Catesby, ere we sleep?

lines.speaker: CATESBY
lines.text: You shall, my lord.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: At Crosby Place, there shall you find us both.
[_Exit Catesby._]

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Now, my lord, what shall we do if we perceive

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Lord Hastings will not yield to our complots?

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Chop off his head, man; somewhat we will do.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And look when I am king, claim thou of me

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: The earldom of Hereford, and all the movables

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Whereof the King my brother was possessed.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: I’ll claim that promise at your Grace’s hand.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And look to have it yielded with all kindness.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Come, let us sup betimes, that afterwards

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: We may digest our complots in some form.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter a Messenger to the door of Hastings.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: My lord, my lord!
[_Knocking._]
[_Within_.]

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: Who knocks?

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: One from the Lord Stanley.
[_Within_.]

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: What is’t o’clock?

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Upon the stroke of four.
Enter Hastings.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: Cannot my Lord Stanley sleep these tedious nights?

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: So it appears by that I have to say.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: First, he commends him to your noble self.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: What then?

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Then certifies your lordship that this night

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: He dreamt the boar had razed off his helm.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Besides, he says there are two councils kept,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: And that may be determined at the one

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Which may make you and him to rue at th’ other.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Therefore he sends to know your lordship’s pleasure,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: If you will presently take horse with him

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: And with all speed post with him toward the north,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: To shun the danger that his soul divines.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: Go, fellow, go. Return unto thy lord;

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: Bid him not fear the separated council.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: His honour and myself are at the one,

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: And at the other is my good friend Catesby,

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: Where nothing can proceed that toucheth us

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: Whereof I shall not have intelligence.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: Tell him his fears are shallow, without instance.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: And for his dreams, I wonder he’s so simple

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: To trust the mockery of unquiet slumbers.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: To fly the boar before the boar pursues

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: Were to incense the boar to follow us,

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: And make pursuit where he did mean no chase.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: Go, bid thy master rise and come to me,

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: And we will both together to the Tower,

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: Where he shall see the boar will use us kindly.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: I’ll go, my lord, and tell him what you say.
[_Exit._]
Enter Catesby.

lines.speaker: CATESBY
lines.text: Many good morrows to my noble lord.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: Good morrow, Catesby; you are early stirring.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: What news, what news in this our tott’ring state?

lines.speaker: CATESBY
lines.text: It is a reeling world indeed, my lord,

lines.speaker: CATESBY
lines.text: And I believe will never stand upright

lines.speaker: CATESBY
lines.text: Till Richard wear the garland of the realm.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: How, wear the garland? Dost thou mean the crown?

lines.speaker: CATESBY
lines.text: Ay, my good lord.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: I’ll have this crown of mine cut from my shoulders

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: Before I’ll see the crown so foul misplaced.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: But canst thou guess that he doth aim at it?

lines.speaker: CATESBY
lines.text: Ay, on my life, and hopes to find you forward

lines.speaker: CATESBY
lines.text: Upon his party for the gain thereof;

lines.speaker: CATESBY
lines.text: And thereupon he sends you this good news,

lines.speaker: CATESBY
lines.text: That this same very day your enemies,

lines.speaker: CATESBY
lines.text: The kindred of the Queen, must die at Pomfret.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: Indeed, I am no mourner for that news,

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: Because they have been still my adversaries.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: But that I’ll give my voice on Richard’s side

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: To bar my master’s heirs in true descent,

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: God knows I will not do it, to the death.

lines.speaker: CATESBY
lines.text: God keep your lordship in that gracious mind.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: But I shall laugh at this a twelve-month hence,

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: That they which brought me in my master’s hate,

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: I live to look upon their tragedy.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: Well, Catesby, ere a fortnight make me older

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: I’ll send some packing that yet think not on’t.

lines.speaker: CATESBY
lines.text: ’Tis a vile thing to die, my gracious lord,

lines.speaker: CATESBY
lines.text: When men are unprepared and look not for it.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: O monstrous, monstrous! And so falls it out

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: With Rivers, Vaughan, Grey; and so ’twill do

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: With some men else that think themselves as safe

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: As thou and I, who, as thou know’st, are dear

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: To princely Richard and to Buckingham.

lines.speaker: CATESBY
lines.text: The Princes both make high account of you—
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: CATESBY
lines.text: For they account his head upon the Bridge.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: I know they do, and I have well deserved it.
Enter Stanley Earl of Derby.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: Come on, come on. Where is your boar-spear, man?

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: Fear you the boar, and go so unprovided?

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: My lord, good morrow; good morrow, Catesby.

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: You may jest on, but, by the Holy Rood,

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: I do not like these several councils, I.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: My lord, I hold my life as dear as you do yours,

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: And never in my days, I do protest,

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: Was it so precious to me as ’tis now.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: Think you, but that I know our state secure,

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: I would be so triumphant as I am?

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: The lords at Pomfret, when they rode from London,

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: Were jocund and supposed their states were sure,

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: And they indeed had no cause to mistrust;

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: But yet you see how soon the day o’ercast.

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: This sudden stab of rancour I misdoubt;

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: Pray God, I say, I prove a needless coward.

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: What, shall we toward the Tower? The day is spent.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: Come, come. Have with you. Wot you what, my lord?

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: Today the lords you talked of are beheaded.

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: They, for their truth, might better wear their heads

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: Than some that have accused them wear their hats.

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: But come, my lord, let’s away.
Enter a Pursuivant.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: Go on before; I’ll talk with this good fellow.
[_Exeunt Stanley and Catesby._]

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: How now, sirrah? How goes the world with thee?

lines.speaker: PURSUIVANT
lines.text: The better that your lordship please to ask.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: I tell thee, man, ’tis better with me now

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: Than when thou met’st me last where now we meet.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: Then was I going prisoner to the Tower,

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: By the suggestion of the Queen’s allies.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: But now, I tell thee—keep it to thyself—

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: This day those enemies are put to death,

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: And I in better state than e’er I was.

lines.speaker: PURSUIVANT
lines.text: God hold it, to your honour’s good content!

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: Gramercy, fellow. There, drink that for me.
[_Throws him his purse._]

lines.speaker: PURSUIVANT
lines.text: I thank your honour.
[_Exit._]
Enter a Priest.

lines.speaker: PRIEST
lines.text: Well met, my lord; I am glad to see your honour.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: I thank thee, good Sir John, with all my heart.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: I am in your debt for your last exercise.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: Come the next sabbath, and I will content you.
Enter Buckingham.

lines.speaker: PRIEST
lines.text: I’ll wait upon your lordship.
[_Exit Priest._]

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: What, talking with a priest, Lord Chamberlain?

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Your friends at Pomfret, they do need the priest;

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Your honour hath no shriving work in hand.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: Good faith, and when I met this holy man,

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: The men you talk of came into my mind.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: What, go you toward the Tower?

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: I do, my lord, but long I cannot stay there.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: I shall return before your lordship thence.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: Nay, like enough, for I stay dinner there.
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: And supper too, although thou knowest it not.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Come, will you go?

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: I’ll wait upon your lordship.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Sir Richard Ratcliffe, with Halberds, carrying the nobles Rivers, Grey and Vaughan to death at Pomfret.

lines.speaker: RIVERS
lines.text: Sir Richard Ratcliffe, let me tell thee this:

lines.speaker: RIVERS
lines.text: Today shalt thou behold a subject die

lines.speaker: RIVERS
lines.text: For truth, for duty, and for loyalty.

lines.speaker: GREY
lines.text: God bless the Prince from all the pack of you!

lines.speaker: GREY
lines.text: A knot you are of damned bloodsuckers.

lines.speaker: GREY
lines.text: VAUGHAN

lines.speaker: GREY
lines.text: You live that shall cry woe for this hereafter.

lines.speaker: GREY
lines.text: RATCLIFFE

lines.speaker: GREY
lines.text: Dispatch. The limit of your lives is out.

lines.speaker: RIVERS
lines.text: O Pomfret, Pomfret! O thou bloody prison,

lines.speaker: RIVERS
lines.text: Fatal and ominous to noble peers!

lines.speaker: RIVERS
lines.text: Within the guilty closure of thy walls

lines.speaker: RIVERS
lines.text: Richard the Second here was hacked to death;

lines.speaker: RIVERS
lines.text: And, for more slander to thy dismal seat,

lines.speaker: RIVERS
lines.text: We give to thee our guiltless blood to drink.

lines.speaker: GREY
lines.text: Now Margaret’s curse is fall’n upon our heads,

lines.speaker: GREY
lines.text: When she exclaimed on Hastings, you, and I,

lines.speaker: GREY
lines.text: For standing by when Richard stabbed her son.

lines.speaker: RIVERS
lines.text: Then cursed she Richard, then cursed she Buckingham,

lines.speaker: RIVERS
lines.text: Then cursed she Hastings. O, remember, God,

lines.speaker: RIVERS
lines.text: To hear her prayer for them, as now for us!

lines.speaker: RIVERS
lines.text: And for my sister and her princely sons,

lines.speaker: RIVERS
lines.text: Be satisfied, dear God, with our true blood,

lines.speaker: RIVERS
lines.text: Which, as thou know’st, unjustly must be spilt.

lines.speaker: RATCLIFFE
lines.text: Make haste. The hour of death is expiate.

lines.speaker: RIVERS
lines.text: Come, Grey, come, Vaughan, let us here embrace.

lines.speaker: RIVERS
lines.text: Farewell, until we meet again in heaven.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: London. A Room in the Tower

lines.text: Enter Buckingham, Stanley Earl of Derby, Hastings, the Bishop of Ely, Norfolk, Ratcliffe, Lovell with others, at a table.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: Now, noble peers, the cause why we are met

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: Is to determine of the coronation.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: In God’s name speak. When is the royal day?

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Is all things ready for that royal time?

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: It is, and wants but nomination.

lines.speaker: ELY
lines.text: Tomorrow, then, I judge a happy day.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Who knows the Lord Protector’s mind herein?

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Who is most inward with the noble Duke?

lines.speaker: ELY
lines.text: Your Grace, we think, should soonest know his mind.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: We know each other’s faces; for our hearts,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: He knows no more of mine than I of yours,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Or I of his, my lord, than you of mine.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Lord Hastings, you and he are near in love.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: I thank his Grace, I know he loves me well;

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: But for his purpose in the coronation

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: I have not sounded him, nor he delivered

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: His gracious pleasure any way therein.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: But you, my honourable lords, may name the time,

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: And in the Duke’s behalf I’ll give my voice,

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: Which I presume he’ll take in gentle part.
Enter Richard.

lines.speaker: ELY
lines.text: In happy time, here comes the Duke himself.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: My noble lords and cousins all, good morrow.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: I have been long a sleeper; but I trust

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: My absence doth neglect no great design

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Which by my presence might have been concluded.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Had you not come upon your cue, my lord,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: William Lord Hastings had pronounced your part—

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: I mean your voice for crowning of the King.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Than my Lord Hastings no man might be bolder.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: His lordship knows me well and loves me well.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: My lord of Ely, when I was last in Holborn

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: I saw good strawberries in your garden there;

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: I do beseech you, send for some of them.

lines.speaker: ELY
lines.text: Marry, and will, my lord, with all my heart.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Cousin of Buckingham, a word with you.
[_They move aside._]

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Catesby hath sounded Hastings in our business,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And finds the testy gentleman so hot

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: That he will lose his head ere give consent

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: His master’s child, as worshipfully he terms it,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Shall lose the royalty of England’s throne.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Withdraw yourself awhile. I’ll go with you.
[_Exeunt Richard and Buckingham._]

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: We have not yet set down this day of triumph.

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: Tomorrow, in my judgement, is too sudden,

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: For I myself am not so well provided

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: As else I would be, were the day prolonged.
Enter Bishop of Ely.

lines.speaker: ELY
lines.text: Where is my lord the Duke of Gloucester?

lines.speaker: ELY
lines.text: I have sent for these strawberries.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: His Grace looks cheerfully and smooth this morning.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: There’s some conceit or other likes him well

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: When that he bids good morrow with such spirit.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: I think there’s never a man in Christendom

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: Can lesser hide his love or hate than he,

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: For by his face straight shall you know his heart.

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: What of his heart perceive you in his face

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: By any livelihood he showed today?

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: Marry, that with no man here he is offended,

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: For were he, he had shown it in his looks.
Enter Richard and Buckingham.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: I pray you all, tell me what they deserve

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: That do conspire my death with devilish plots

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Of damned witchcraft, and that have prevailed

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Upon my body with their hellish charms?

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: The tender love I bear your Grace, my lord,

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: Makes me most forward in this princely presence

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: To doom th’ offenders, whosoe’er they be.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: I say, my lord, they have deserved death.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Then be your eyes the witness of their evil.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Look how I am bewitched! Behold, mine arm

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Is like a blasted sapling withered up!

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And this is Edward’s wife, that monstrous witch,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Consorted with that harlot, strumpet Shore,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: That by their witchcraft thus have marked me.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: If they have done this deed, my noble lord—

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: If? Thou protector of this damned strumpet,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Talk’st thou to me of “ifs”? Thou art a traitor.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Off with his head! Now by Saint Paul I swear

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: I will not dine until I see the same.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Lovell and Ratcliffe, look that it be done.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: The rest that love me, rise and follow me.
[_Exeunt all but Lovell and Ratcliffe with the Lord Hastings._]

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: Woe, woe, for England! Not a whit for me,

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: For I, too fond, might have prevented this.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: Stanley did dream the boar did raze his helm,

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: And I did scorn it and disdain to fly.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: Three times today my foot-cloth horse did stumble,

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: And started when he looked upon the Tower,

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: As loath to bear me to the slaughter-house.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: O, now I need the priest that spake to me;

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: I now repent I told the pursuivant,

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: As too triumphing, how mine enemies

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: Today at Pomfret bloodily were butchered,

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: And I myself secure in grace and favour.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: O Margaret, Margaret, now thy heavy curse

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: Is lighted on poor Hastings’ wretched head.

lines.speaker: RATCLIFFE
lines.text: Come, come, dispatch. The Duke would be at dinner:

lines.speaker: RATCLIFFE
lines.text: Make a short shrift. He longs to see your head.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: O momentary grace of mortal men,

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: Which we more hunt for than the grace of God!

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: Who builds his hope in air of your good looks

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: Lives like a drunken sailor on a mast,

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: Ready with every nod to tumble down

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: Into the fatal bowels of the deep.

lines.speaker: LOVELL
lines.text: Come, come, dispatch. ’Tis bootless to exclaim.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: O bloody Richard! Miserable England,

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: I prophesy the fearfull’st time to thee

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: That ever wretched age hath looked upon.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: Come, lead me to the block. Bear him my head.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: They smile at me who shortly shall be dead.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Richard and Buckingham in rotten armour, marvellous ill-favoured.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Come, cousin, canst thou quake and change thy colour,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Murder thy breath in middle of a word,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And then again begin, and stop again,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: As if thou were distraught and mad with terror?

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Tut, I can counterfeit the deep tragedian;

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Speak, and look back, and pry on every side,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Tremble and start at wagging of a straw,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Intending deep suspicion. Ghastly looks

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Are at my service, like enforced smiles,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: And both are ready in their offices,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: At anytime to grace my stratagems.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: But what, is Catesby gone?

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: He is; and, see, he brings the Mayor along.
Enter the Lord Mayor and Catesby.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Lord Mayor—

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Look to the drawbridge there!

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Hark, a drum.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Catesby, o’erlook the walls.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Lord Mayor, the reason we have sent—

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Look back! Defend thee, here are enemies.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: God and our innocence defend and guard us!
Enter Lovell and Ratcliffe with Hastings’ head.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Be patient, they are friends, Ratcliffe and Lovell.

lines.speaker: LOVELL
lines.text: Here is the head of that ignoble traitor,

lines.speaker: LOVELL
lines.text: The dangerous and unsuspected Hastings.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: So dear I loved the man that I must weep.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: I took him for the plainest harmless creature

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: That breathed upon the earth a Christian;

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Made him my book, wherein my soul recorded

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: The history of all her secret thoughts.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: So smooth he daubed his vice with show of virtue

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: That, his apparent open guilt omitted—

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: I mean his conversation with Shore’s wife—

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: He lived from all attainder of suspects.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Well, well, he was the covert’st sheltered traitor

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: That ever lived.—

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Would you imagine, or almost believe,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Were’t not that by great preservation

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: We live to tell it, that the subtle traitor

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: This day had plotted, in the council-house,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: To murder me and my good lord of Gloucester?

lines.speaker: MAYOR
lines.text: Had he done so?

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: What, think you we are Turks or Infidels?

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Or that we would, against the form of law,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Proceed thus rashly in the villain’s death,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: But that the extreme peril of the case,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: The peace of England, and our persons’ safety,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Enforced us to this execution?

lines.speaker: MAYOR
lines.text: Now, fair befall you! He deserved his death,

lines.speaker: MAYOR
lines.text: And your good Graces both have well proceeded,

lines.speaker: MAYOR
lines.text: To warn false traitors from the like attempts.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: I never looked for better at his hands

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: After he once fell in with Mistress Shore.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Yet had we not determined he should die

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Until your lordship came to see his end

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Which now the loving haste of these our friends,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Something against our meanings, have prevented,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Because, my lord, we would have had you heard

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: The traitor speak, and timorously confess

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: The manner and the purpose of his treasons,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: That you might well have signified the same

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Unto the citizens, who haply may

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Misconster us in him, and wail his death.

lines.speaker: MAYOR
lines.text: But, my good lord, your Grace’s word shall serve

lines.speaker: MAYOR
lines.text: As well as I had seen and heard him speak;

lines.speaker: MAYOR
lines.text: And do not doubt, right noble princes both,

lines.speaker: MAYOR
lines.text: But I’ll acquaint our duteous citizens

lines.speaker: MAYOR
lines.text: With all your just proceedings in this case.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And to that end we wished your lordship here,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: T’ avoid the censures of the carping world.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: But since you come too late of our intent,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Yet witness what you hear we did intend.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: And so, my good Lord Mayor, we bid farewell.
[_Exit Lord Mayor._]

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Go, after, after, cousin Buckingham.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: The Mayor towards Guildhall hies him in all post.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: There, at your meet’st advantage of the time,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Infer the bastardy of Edward’s children;

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Tell them how Edward put to death a citizen

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Only for saying he would make his son

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Heir to the Crown—meaning indeed his house,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Which, by the sign thereof, was termed so.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Moreover, urge his hateful luxury

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And bestial appetite in change of lust,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Which stretched unto their servants, daughters, wives,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Even where his raging eye or savage heart,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Without control, lusted to make a prey.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Nay, for a need, thus far come near my person:

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Tell them, when that my mother went with child

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Of that insatiate Edward, noble York

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: My princely father then had wars in France,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And, by true computation of the time,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Found that the issue was not his begot;

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Which well appeared in his lineaments,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Being nothing like the noble Duke, my father.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Yet touch this sparingly, as ’twere far off;

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Because, my lord, you know my mother lives.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Doubt not, my lord, I’ll play the orator

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: As if the golden fee for which I plead

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Were for myself. And so, my lord, adieu.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: If you thrive well, bring them to Baynard’s Castle,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Where you shall find me well accompanied

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: With reverend fathers and well-learned bishops.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: I go; and towards three or four o’clock

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Look for the news that the Guildhall affords.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Go, Lovell, with all speed to Doctor Shaa.
[_To Ratcliffe_.]

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Go thou to Friar Penker; bid them both

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Meet me within this hour at Baynard’s Castle.
[_Exeunt Ratcliffe and Lovell._]

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Now will I go to take some privy order

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: To draw the brats of Clarence out of sight,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And to give order that no manner person

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Have any time recourse unto the Princes.
[_Exit._]
Enter a Scrivener.

lines.speaker: SCRIVENER
lines.text: Here is the indictment of the good Lord Hastings,

lines.speaker: SCRIVENER
lines.text: Which in a set hand fairly is engrossed,

lines.speaker: SCRIVENER
lines.text: That it may be today read o’er in Paul’s.

lines.speaker: SCRIVENER
lines.text: And mark how well the sequel hangs together:

lines.speaker: SCRIVENER
lines.text: Eleven hours I have spent to write it over,

lines.speaker: SCRIVENER
lines.text: For yesternight by Catesby was it sent me;

lines.speaker: SCRIVENER
lines.text: The precedent was full as long a-doing

lines.speaker: SCRIVENER
lines.text: And yet within these five hours Hastings lived,

lines.speaker: SCRIVENER
lines.text: Untainted, unexamined, free, at liberty.

lines.speaker: SCRIVENER
lines.text: Here’s a good world the while! Who is so gross

lines.speaker: SCRIVENER
lines.text: That cannot see this palpable device?

lines.speaker: SCRIVENER
lines.text: Yet who so bold but says he sees it not?

lines.speaker: SCRIVENER
lines.text: Bad is the world, and all will come to naught

lines.speaker: SCRIVENER
lines.text: When such ill dealing must be seen in thought.
[_Exit._]
Enter Richard and Buckingham at several doors.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: How now, how now? What say the citizens?

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Now, by the holy mother of our Lord,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: The citizens are mum, say not a word.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Touched you the bastardy of Edward’s children?

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: I did; with his contract with Lady Lucy,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: And his contract by deputy in France;

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Th’ insatiate greediness of his desire,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: And his enforcement of the city wives;

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: His tyranny for trifles; his own bastardy,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: As being got, your father then in France,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: And his resemblance, being not like the Duke.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Withal, I did infer your lineaments,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Being the right idea of your father,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Both in your form and nobleness of mind;

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Laid open all your victories in Scotland,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Your discipline in war, wisdom in peace,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Your bounty, virtue, fair humility;

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Indeed, left nothing fitting for your purpose

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Untouched or slightly handled in discourse.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: And when mine oratory drew toward end,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: I bid them that did love their country’s good

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Cry “God save Richard, England’s royal King!”

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And did they so?

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: No, so God help me, they spake not a word,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: But, like dumb statues or breathing stones,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Stared each on other, and looked deadly pale.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Which when I saw, I reprehended them,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: And asked the Mayor what meant this wilful silence.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: His answer was, the people were not used

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: To be spoke to but by the Recorder.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Then he was urged to tell my tale again:

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: “Thus saith the Duke, thus hath the Duke inferred”

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: But nothing spoke in warrant from himself.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: When he had done, some followers of mine own,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: At lower end of the hall, hurled up their caps,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: And some ten voices cried, “God save King Richard!”

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: And thus I took the vantage of those few.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: “Thanks, gentle citizens and friends,” quoth I;

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: “This general applause and cheerful shout

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Argues your wisdoms and your love to Richard.”

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: And even here brake off and came away.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: What, tongueless blocks were they! Would they not speak?

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Will not the Mayor then and his brethren, come?

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: The mayor is here at hand. Intend some fear;

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Be not you spoke with but by mighty suit.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: And look you get a prayer-book in your hand,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: And stand between two churchmen, good my lord,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: For on that ground I’ll make a holy descant.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: And be not easily won to our requests.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Play the maid’s part: still answer nay, and take it.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: I go, and if you plead as well for them

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: As I can say nay to thee for myself,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: No doubt we bring it to a happy issue.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Go, go, up to the leads, the Lord Mayor knocks.
[_Exit Richard._]
Enter the Lord Mayor and Citizens.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Welcome, my lord. I dance attendance here.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: I think the Duke will not be spoke withal.
Enter Catesby.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Now, Catesby, what says your lord to my request?

lines.speaker: CATESBY
lines.text: He doth entreat your Grace, my noble lord,

lines.speaker: CATESBY
lines.text: To visit him tomorrow or next day.

lines.speaker: CATESBY
lines.text: He is within, with two right reverend fathers,

lines.speaker: CATESBY
lines.text: Divinely bent to meditation;

lines.speaker: CATESBY
lines.text: And in no worldly suits would he be moved

lines.speaker: CATESBY
lines.text: To draw him from his holy exercise.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Return, good Catesby, to the gracious Duke;

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Tell him myself, the Mayor and aldermen,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: In deep designs, in matter of great moment,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: No less importing than our general good,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Are come to have some conference with his Grace.

lines.speaker: CATESBY
lines.text: I’ll signify so much unto him straight.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Ah ha, my lord, this prince is not an Edward!

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: He is not lolling on a lewd love-bed,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: But on his knees at meditation;

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Not dallying with a brace of courtesans,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: But meditating with two deep divines;

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Not sleeping, to engross his idle body,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: But praying, to enrich his watchful soul.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Happy were England would this virtuous prince

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Take on his Grace the sovereignty thereof.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: But sure I fear we shall not win him to it.

lines.speaker: MAYOR
lines.text: Marry, God defend his Grace should say us nay!

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: I fear he will. Here Catesby comes again.
Enter Catesby.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Now, Catesby, what says his Grace?

lines.speaker: CATESBY
lines.text: He wonders to what end you have assembled

lines.speaker: CATESBY
lines.text: Such troops of citizens to come to him,

lines.speaker: CATESBY
lines.text: His Grace not being warned thereof before.

lines.speaker: CATESBY
lines.text: He fears, my lord, you mean no good to him.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Sorry I am my noble cousin should

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Suspect me that I mean no good to him.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: By heaven, we come to him in perfect love,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: And so once more return and tell his Grace.
[_Exit Catesby._]

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: When holy and devout religious men

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Are at their beads, ’tis much to draw them thence,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: So sweet is zealous contemplation.
Enter Richard aloft, between two Bishops. Catesby reenters.

lines.speaker: MAYOR
lines.text: See where his Grace stands ’tween two clergymen!

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Two props of virtue for a Christian prince,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: To stay him from the fall of vanity;

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: And, see, a book of prayer in his hand,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: True ornaments to know a holy man.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Famous Plantagenet, most gracious Prince,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Lend favourable ear to our requests,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: And pardon us the interruption

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Of thy devotion and right Christian zeal.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: My lord, there needs no such apology.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: I do beseech your Grace to pardon me,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Who, earnest in the service of my God,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Deferred the visitation of my friends.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: But, leaving this, what is your Grace’s pleasure?

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Even that, I hope, which pleaseth God above,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: And all good men of this ungoverned isle.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: I do suspect I have done some offence

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: That seems disgracious in the city’s eye,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And that you come to reprehend my ignorance.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: You have, my lord. Would it might please your Grace,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: On our entreaties, to amend your fault.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Else wherefore breathe I in a Christian land?

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Know then, it is your fault that you resign

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: The supreme seat, the throne majestical,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: The sceptered office of your ancestors,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Your state of fortune, and your due of birth,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: The lineal glory of your royal house,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: To the corruption of a blemished stock;

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Whiles in the mildness of your sleepy thoughts,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Which here we waken to our country’s good,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: The noble isle doth want her proper limbs;

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Her face defaced with scars of infamy,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Her royal stock graft with ignoble plants,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: And almost shouldered in the swallowing gulf

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Of dark forgetfulness and deep oblivion;

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Which to recure, we heartily solicit

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Your gracious self to take on you the charge

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: And kingly government of this your land,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Not as Protector, steward, substitute,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Or lowly factor for another’s gain,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: But as successively, from blood to blood,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Your right of birth, your empery, your own.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: For this, consorted with the citizens,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Your very worshipful and loving friends,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: And by their vehement instigation,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: In this just cause come I to move your Grace.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: I cannot tell if to depart in silence

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Or bitterly to speak in your reproof

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Best fitteth my degree or your condition.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: If not to answer, you might haply think

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Tongue-tied ambition, not replying, yielded

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: To bear the golden yoke of sovereignty,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Which fondly you would here impose on me;

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: If to reprove you for this suit of yours,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: So seasoned with your faithful love to me,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Then, on the other side, I checked my friends.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Therefore, to speak, and to avoid the first,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And then, in speaking, not to incur the last,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Definitively thus I answer you:

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Your love deserves my thanks, but my desert

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Unmeritable shuns your high request.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: First, if all obstacles were cut away,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And that my path were even to the crown

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: As the ripe revenue and due of birth,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Yet so much is my poverty of spirit,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: So mighty and so many my defects,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: That I would rather hide me from my greatness,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Being a bark to brook no mighty sea,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Than in my greatness covet to be hid,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And in the vapour of my glory smothered.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: But, God be thanked, there is no need of me,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And much I need to help you, were there need.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: The royal tree hath left us royal fruit,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Which, mellowed by the stealing hours of time,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Will well become the seat of majesty,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: And make, no doubt, us happy by his reign.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: On him I lay that you would lay on me,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: The right and fortune of his happy stars,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Which God defend that I should wring from him.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: My lord, this argues conscience in your Grace;

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: But the respects thereof are nice and trivial,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: All circumstances well considered.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: You say that Edward is your brother’s son;

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: So say we too, but not by Edward’s wife.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: For first was he contract to Lady Lucy

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Your mother lives a witness to his vow,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: And afterward by substitute betrothed

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: To Bona, sister to the King of France.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: These both put off, a poor petitioner,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: A care-crazed mother to a many sons,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: A beauty-waning and distressed widow,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Even in the afternoon of her best days,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Made prize and purchase of his wanton eye,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Seduced the pitch and height of his degree

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: To base declension and loathed bigamy.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: By her, in his unlawful bed, he got

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: This Edward, whom our manners call the Prince.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: More bitterly could I expostulate,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Save that, for reverence to some alive,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: I give a sparing limit to my tongue.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Then, good my lord, take to your royal self

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: This proffered benefit of dignity,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: If not to bless us and the land withal,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Yet to draw forth your noble ancestry

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: From the corruption of abusing times

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Unto a lineal true-derived course.

lines.speaker: MAYOR
lines.text: Do, good my lord. Your citizens entreat you.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Refuse not, mighty lord, this proffered love.

lines.speaker: CATESBY
lines.text: O, make them joyful; grant their lawful suit.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Alas, why would you heap those cares on me?

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: I am unfit for state and majesty.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: I do beseech you, take it not amiss;

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: I cannot, nor I will not, yield to you.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: If you refuse it, as in love and zeal

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Loath to depose the child, your brother’s son—

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: As well we know your tenderness of heart

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: And gentle, kind, effeminate remorse,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Which we have noted in you to your kindred,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: And equally indeed to all estates—

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Yet know, whe’er you accept our suit or no,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Your brother’s son shall never reign our king,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: But we will plant some other in the throne,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: To the disgrace and downfall of your house.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: And in this resolution here we leave you.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Come, citizens; zounds, I’ll entreat no more.
[_Exeunt Buckingham, the Mayor and citizens._]

lines.speaker: CATESBY
lines.text: Call him again, sweet Prince; accept their suit.

lines.speaker: CATESBY
lines.text: If you deny them, all the land will rue it.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Will you enforce me to a world of cares?

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Call them again. I am not made of stones,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: But penetrable to your kind entreaties,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Albeit against my conscience and my soul.
Enter Buckingham and the rest.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Cousin of Buckingham, and sage grave men,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Since you will buckle Fortune on my back,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: To bear her burden, whe’er I will or no,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: I must have patience to endure the load.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: But if black scandal or foul-faced reproach

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Attend the sequel of your imposition,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Your mere enforcement shall acquittance me

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: From all the impure blots and stains thereof,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: For God doth know, and you may partly see,

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: How far I am from the desire of this.

lines.speaker: MAYOR
lines.text: God bless your Grace! We see it, and will say it.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: In saying so, you shall but say the truth.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Then I salute you with this royal title:

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Long live King Richard, England’s worthy King!

lines.speaker: ALL
lines.text: Amen.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Tomorrow may it please you to be crowned?

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Even when you please, for you will have it so.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Tomorrow, then, we will attend your Grace;

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: And so most joyfully we take our leave.
[_To the Bishops_.]

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Come, let us to our holy work again.

lines.speaker: RICHARD
lines.text: Farewell, my cousin, farewell, gentle friends.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Queen Elizabeth, the Duchess of York and Marquess of Dorset, at one door; Anne Duchess of Gloucester with Clarence’s young Daughter at another door.

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: Who meets us here? My niece Plantagenet

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: Led in the hand of her kind aunt of Gloucester?

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: Now, for my life, she’s wandering to the Tower,

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: On pure heart’s love, to greet the tender Prince.

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: Daughter, well met.

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: God give your Graces both

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: A happy and a joyful time of day.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: As much to you, good sister. Whither away?

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: No farther than the Tower, and, as I guess,

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: Upon the like devotion as yourselves,

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: To gratulate the gentle Princes there.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Kind sister, thanks; we’ll enter all together.
Enter Brakenbury.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: And in good time, here the Lieutenant comes.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Master Lieutenant, pray you, by your leave,

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: How doth the Prince and my young son of York?

lines.speaker: BRAKENBURY
lines.text: Right well, dear madam. By your patience,

lines.speaker: BRAKENBURY
lines.text: I may not suffer you to visit them.

lines.speaker: BRAKENBURY
lines.text: The King hath strictly charged the contrary.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: The King? Who’s that?

lines.speaker: BRAKENBURY
lines.text: I mean the Lord Protector.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: The Lord protect him from that kingly title!

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Hath he set bounds between their love and me?

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: I am their mother; who shall bar me from them?

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: I am their father’s mother. I will see them.

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: Their aunt I am in law, in love their mother.

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: Then bring me to their sights. I’ll bear thy blame,

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: And take thy office from thee, on my peril.

lines.speaker: BRAKENBURY
lines.text: No, madam, no. I may not leave it so.

lines.speaker: BRAKENBURY
lines.text: I am bound by oath, and therefore pardon me.
[_Exit._]
Enter Stanley.

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: Let me but meet you, ladies, one hour hence,

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: And I’ll salute your Grace of York as mother

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: And reverend looker-on of two fair queens.
[_To Anne._]

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: Come, madam, you must straight to Westminster,

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: There to be crowned Richard’s royal queen.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Ah, cut my lace asunder

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: That my pent heart may have some scope to beat,

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Or else I swoon with this dead-killing news!

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: Despiteful tidings! O unpleasing news!

lines.speaker: DORSET
lines.text: Be of good cheer, mother. How fares your Grace?

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: O Dorset, speak not to me; get thee gone.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Death and destruction dog thee at thy heels;

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Thy mother’s name is ominous to children.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: If thou wilt outstrip death, go, cross the seas,

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: And live with Richmond, from the reach of hell.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Go, hie thee, hie thee from this slaughter-house,

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Lest thou increase the number of the dead,

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: And make me die the thrall of Margaret’s curse,

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
