lines.text: Nor mother, wife, nor England’s counted Queen.

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: Full of wise care is this your counsel, madam.

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: Take all the swift advantage of the hours;

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: You shall have letters from me to my son

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: In your behalf, to meet you on the way.

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: Be not ta’en tardy by unwise delay.

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: O ill-dispersing wind of misery!

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: O my accursed womb, the bed of death!

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: A cockatrice hast thou hatched to the world,

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: Whose unavoided eye is murderous.

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: Come, madam, come. I in all haste was sent.

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: And I with all unwillingness will go.

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: O, would to God that the inclusive verge

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: Of golden metal that must round my brow

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: Were red-hot steel, to sear me to the brains.

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: Anointed let me be with deadly venom,

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: And die ere men can say “God save the Queen.”

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Go, go, poor soul; I envy not thy glory.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: To feed my humour, wish thyself no harm.

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: No? Why? When he that is my husband now

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: Came to me as I followed Henry’s corse,

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: When scarce the blood was well washed from his hands

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: Which issued from my other angel husband,

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: And that dear saint which then I weeping followed;

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: O, when, I say, I looked on Richard’s face,

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: This was my wish: “Be thou,” quoth I, “accursed

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: For making me, so young, so old a widow;

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: And when thou wedd’st, let sorrow haunt thy bed;

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: And be thy wife, if any be so mad,

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: More miserable by the life of thee

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: Than thou hast made me by my dear lord’s death.”

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: Lo, ere I can repeat this curse again,

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: Within so small a time, my woman’s heart

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: Grossly grew captive to his honey words,

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: And proved the subject of mine own soul’s curse,

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: Which hitherto hath held my eyes from rest;

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: For never yet one hour in his bed

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: Did I enjoy the golden dew of sleep,

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: But with his timorous dreams was still awaked.

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: Besides, he hates me for my father Warwick,

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: And will, no doubt, shortly be rid of me.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Poor heart, adieu; I pity thy complaining.

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: No more than with my soul I mourn for yours.

lines.speaker: DORSET
lines.text: Farewell, thou woeful welcomer of glory.

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: Adieu, poor soul, that tak’st thy leave of it.
[_To Dorset._]

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: Go thou to Richmond, and good fortune guide thee.
[_To Anne._]

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: Go thou to Richard, and good angels tend thee.
[_To Queen Elizabeth._]

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: Go thou to sanctuary, and good thoughts possess

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: thee.

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: I to my grave, where peace and rest lie with me.

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: Eighty odd years of sorrow have I seen,

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: And each hour’s joy wracked with a week of teen.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Stay, yet look back with me unto the Tower.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Pity, you ancient stones, those tender babes

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Whom envy hath immured within your walls—

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Rough cradle for such little pretty one,

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Rude ragged nurse, old sullen playfellow

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: For tender princes, use my babies well.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: So foolish sorrows bids your stones farewell.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: London. A Room of State in the Palace

lines.text: The trumpets sound a sennet. Enter Richard in pomp, Buckingham, Catesby, Ratcliffe, Lovell, a Page and others.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Stand all apart. Cousin of Buckingham!

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: My gracious sovereign!

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Give me thy hand.
[_Here he ascendeth the throne. Sound trumpets._]

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Thus high, by thy advice

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: And thy assistance is King Richard seated.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: But shall we wear these glories for a day,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Or shall they last, and we rejoice in them?

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Still live they, and for ever let them last!

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Ah, Buckingham, now do I play the touch,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: To try if thou be current gold indeed.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Young Edward lives; think now what I would speak.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Say on, my loving lord.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Why, Buckingham, I say I would be King.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Why, so you are, my thrice-renowned lord.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Ha! Am I King? ’Tis so—but Edward lives.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: True, noble Prince.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: O bitter consequence,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: That Edward still should live “true noble prince!”

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Cousin, thou wast not wont to be so dull.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Shall I be plain? I wish the bastards dead,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: And I would have it suddenly performed.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: What sayst thou now? Speak suddenly, be brief.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Your Grace may do your pleasure.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Tut, tut, thou art all ice; thy kindness freezes.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Say, have I thy consent that they shall die?

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Give me some little breath, some pause, dear lord,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Before I positively speak in this.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: I will resolve you herein presently.
[_Exit._]
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: CATESBY
lines.text: The King is angry. See, he gnaws his lip.
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: I will converse with iron-witted fools

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: And unrespective boys; none are for me

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: That look into me with considerate eyes.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: High-reaching Buckingham grows circumspect.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Boy!

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: My lord?

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Know’st thou not any whom corrupting gold

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Will tempt unto a close exploit of death?

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: I know a discontented gentleman

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: Whose humble means match not his haughty spirit.

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: Gold were as good as twenty orators,

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: And will, no doubt, tempt him to anything.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: What is his name?

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: His name, my lord, is Tyrrel.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: I partly know the man. Go, call him hither, boy.
[_Exit Page._]
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: The deep-revolving witty Buckingham

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: No more shall be the neighbour to my counsels.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Hath he so long held out with me, untired,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: And stops he now for breath? Well, be it so.
Enter Stanley.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: How now, Lord Stanley, what’s the news?

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: Know, my loving lord,

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: The Marquess Dorset, as I hear, is fled

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: To Richmond, in the parts where he abides.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Come hither, Catesby. Rumour it abroad

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: That Anne my wife is very grievous sick;

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: I will take order for her keeping close.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Inquire me out some mean poor gentleman,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Whom I will marry straight to Clarence’ daughter.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: The boy is foolish, and I fear not him.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Look how thou dream’st! I say again, give out

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: That Anne, my Queen, is sick and like to die.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: About it, for it stands me much upon

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: To stop all hopes whose growth may damage me.
[_Exit Catesby._]

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: I must be married to my brother’s daughter,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Or else my kingdom stands on brittle glass.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Murder her brothers, and then marry her—

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Uncertain way of gain! But I am in

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: So far in blood that sin will pluck on sin.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Tear-falling pity dwells not in this eye.
Enter Tyrrel.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Is thy name Tyrrel?

lines.speaker: TYRREL
lines.text: James Tyrrel, and your most obedient subject.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Art thou indeed?

lines.speaker: TYRREL
lines.text: Prove me, my gracious lord.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Dar’st thou resolve to kill a friend of mine?

lines.speaker: TYRREL
lines.text: Please you. But I had rather kill two enemies.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Why then thou hast it; two deep enemies,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Foes to my rest, and my sweet sleep’s disturbers,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Are they that I would have thee deal upon.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Tyrell, I mean those bastards in the Tower.

lines.speaker: TYRREL
lines.text: Let me have open means to come to them,

lines.speaker: TYRREL
lines.text: And soon I’ll rid you from the fear of them.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Thou sing’st sweet music. Hark, come hither, Tyrrel.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Go, by this token. Rise, and lend thine ear.
[_Whispers_.]

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: There is no more but so. Say it is done,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: And I will love thee, and prefer thee for it.

lines.speaker: TYRREL
lines.text: I will dispatch it straight.
[_Exit._]
Enter Buckingham.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: My lord, I have considered in my mind

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: The late request that you did sound me in.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Well, let that rest. Dorset is fled to Richmond.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: I hear the news, my lord.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Stanley, he is your wife’s son. Well, look unto it.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: My lord, I claim the gift, my due by promise,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: For which your honour and your faith is pawned:

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Th’ earldom of Hereford, and the movables

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Which you have promised I shall possess.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Stanley, look to your wife. If she convey

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Letters to Richmond, you shall answer it.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: What says your Highness to my just request?

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: I do remember me, Henry the Sixth

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Did prophesy that Richmond should be King,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: When Richmond was a little peevish boy.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: A king perhaps—

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: My lord—

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: How chance the prophet could not at that time

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Have told me, I being by, that I should kill him?

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: My lord, your promise for the earldom—

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Richmond! When last I was at Exeter,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: The Mayor in courtesy showed me the castle

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: And called it Rougemount, at which name I started,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Because a bard of Ireland told me once

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: I should not live long after I saw Richmond.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: My lord—

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Ay, what’s o’clock?

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: I am thus bold to put your Grace in mind

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Of what you promised me.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Well, but what’s o’clock?

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Upon the stroke of ten.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Well, let it strike.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Why let it strike?

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Because that, like a jack, thou keep’st the stroke

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Betwixt thy begging and my meditation.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: I am not in the giving vein today.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Why then, resolve me whether you will or no.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Thou troublest me; I am not in the vein.
[_Exit followed by all save Buckingham._]

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: And is it thus? Repays he my deep service

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: With such contempt? Made I him King for this?

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: O, let me think on Hastings, and be gone

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: To Brecknock while my fearful head is on!
[_Exit._]

scenes.setting: London. Another Room in the Palace

lines.text: Enter Tyrrel.

lines.speaker: TYRREL
lines.text: The tyrannous and bloody act is done,

lines.speaker: TYRREL
lines.text: The most arch deed of piteous massacre

lines.speaker: TYRREL
lines.text: That ever yet this land was guilty of.

lines.speaker: TYRREL
lines.text: Dighton and Forrest, who I did suborn

lines.speaker: TYRREL
lines.text: To do this piece of ruthless butchery,

lines.speaker: TYRREL
lines.text: Albeit they were fleshed villains, bloody dogs,

lines.speaker: TYRREL
lines.text: Melted with tenderness and mild compassion,

lines.speaker: TYRREL
lines.text: Wept like two children in their deaths’ sad story.

lines.speaker: TYRREL
lines.text: “O, thus,” quoth Dighton, “lay the gentle babes;”

lines.speaker: TYRREL
lines.text: “Thus, thus,” quoth Forrest, “girdling one another

lines.speaker: TYRREL
lines.text: Within their alabaster innocent arms.

lines.speaker: TYRREL
lines.text: Their lips were four red roses on a stalk,

lines.speaker: TYRREL
lines.text: And in their summer beauty kissed each other.

lines.speaker: TYRREL
lines.text: A book of prayers on their pillow lay,

lines.speaker: TYRREL
lines.text: Which once,” quoth Forrest, “almost changed my mind.

lines.speaker: TYRREL
lines.text: But, O, the devil—” There the villain stopped;

lines.speaker: TYRREL
lines.text: When Dighton thus told on: “We smothered

lines.speaker: TYRREL
lines.text: The most replenished sweet work of nature

lines.speaker: TYRREL
lines.text: That from the prime creation e’er she framed.”

lines.speaker: TYRREL
lines.text: Hence both are gone with conscience and remorse

lines.speaker: TYRREL
lines.text: They could not speak; and so I left them both

lines.speaker: TYRREL
lines.text: To bear this tidings to the bloody King.
Enter King Richard.

lines.speaker: TYRREL
lines.text: And here he comes. All health, my sovereign lord.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Kind Tyrrel, am I happy in thy news?

lines.speaker: TYRREL
lines.text: If to have done the thing you gave in charge

lines.speaker: TYRREL
lines.text: Beget your happiness, be happy then,

lines.speaker: TYRREL
lines.text: For it is done.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: But didst thou see them dead?

lines.speaker: TYRREL
lines.text: I did, my lord.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: And buried, gentle Tyrrel?

lines.speaker: TYRREL
lines.text: The chaplain of the Tower hath buried them,

lines.speaker: TYRREL
lines.text: But where, to say the truth, I do not know.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Come to me, Tyrrel, soon, at after-supper,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: When thou shalt tell the process of their death.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Meantime, but think how I may do thee good,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: And be inheritor of thy desire.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Farewell till then.

lines.speaker: TYRREL
lines.text: I humbly take my leave.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: The son of Clarence have I pent up close;

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: His daughter meanly have I matched in marriage;

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: The sons of Edward sleep in Abraham’s bosom,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: And Anne my wife hath bid the world good night.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Now, for I know the Breton Richmond aims

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: At young Elizabeth, my brother’s daughter,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: And by that knot looks proudly on the crown,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: To her go I, a jolly thriving wooer.
Enter Ratcliffe.

lines.speaker: RATCLIFFE
lines.text: My lord!

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Good or bad news, that thou com’st in so bluntly?

lines.speaker: RATCLIFFE
lines.text: Bad news, my lord. Morton is fled to Richmond,

lines.speaker: RATCLIFFE
lines.text: And Buckingham, backed with the hardy Welshmen,

lines.speaker: RATCLIFFE
lines.text: Is in the field, and still his power increaseth.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Ely with Richmond troubles me more near

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Than Buckingham and his rash-levied strength.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Come, I have learned that fearful commenting

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Is leaden servitor to dull delay;

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Delay leads impotent and snail-paced beggary;

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Then fiery expedition be my wing,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Jove’s Mercury, and herald for a king!

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Go, muster men. My counsel is my shield.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: We must be brief when traitors brave the field.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter old Queen Margaret.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: So now prosperity begins to mellow,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And drop into the rotten mouth of death.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Here in these confines slily have I lurked

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: To watch the waning of mine enemies.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: A dire induction am I witness to,

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: And will to France, hoping the consequence

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Will prove as bitter, black, and tragical.

lines.speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
lines.text: Withdraw thee, wretched Margaret. Who comes here?
[_Retires._]
Enter Duchess of York and Queen Elizabeth.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Ah, my poor Princes! Ah, my tender babes,

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: My unblown flowers, new-appearing sweets!

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: If yet your gentle souls fly in the air

lines.text: Mad’st quick conveyance with her good aunt Anne.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: You mock me, madam; this is not the way

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: To win your daughter.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: There is no other way,

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Unless thou couldst put on some other shape,

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: And not be Richard, that hath done all this.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Say that I did all this for love of her?

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Nay, then indeed she cannot choose but hate thee,

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Having bought love with such a bloody spoil.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Look what is done cannot be now amended.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Men shall deal unadvisedly sometimes,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Which after-hours gives leisure to repent.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: If I did take the kingdom from your sons,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: To make amends I’ll give it to your daughter.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: If I have killed the issue of your womb,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: To quicken your increase I will beget

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Mine issue of your blood upon your daughter.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: A grandam’s name is little less in love

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Than is the doting title of a mother;

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: They are as children but one step below,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Even of your mettle, of your very blood;

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Of all one pain, save for a night of groans

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Endured of her, for whom you bid like sorrow.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Your children were vexation to your youth,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: But mine shall be a comfort to your age.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: The loss you have is but a son being King,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: And by that loss your daughter is made Queen.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: I cannot make you what amends I would;

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Therefore accept such kindness as I can.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Dorset your son, that with a fearful soul

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Leads discontented steps in foreign soil,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: This fair alliance quickly shall call home

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: To high promotions and great dignity.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: The King, that calls your beauteous daughter wife,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Familiarly shall call thy Dorset brother;

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Again shall you be mother to a king,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: And all the ruins of distressful times

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Repaired with double riches of content.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: What, we have many goodly days to see.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: The liquid drops of tears that you have shed

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Shall come again, transformed to orient pearl,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Advantaging their loan with interest

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Of ten times double gain of happiness.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Go then, my mother, to thy daughter go.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Make bold her bashful years with your experience;

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Prepare her ears to hear a wooer’s tale;

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Put in her tender heart th’ aspiring flame

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Of golden sovereignty; acquaint the Princess

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: With the sweet silent hours of marriage joys,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: And when this arm of mine hath chastised

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: The petty rebel, dull-brained Buckingham,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Bound with triumphant garlands will I come

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: And lead thy daughter to a conqueror’s bed;

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: To whom I will retail my conquest won,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: And she shall be sole victoress, Caesar’s Caesar.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: What were I best to say? Her father’s brother

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Would be her lord? Or shall I say her uncle?

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Or he that slew her brothers and her uncles?

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Under what title shall I woo for thee,

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: That God, the law, my honour, and her love

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Can make seem pleasing to her tender years?

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Infer fair England’s peace by this alliance.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Which she shall purchase with still-lasting war.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Tell her the King, that may command, entreats.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: That at her hands, which the King’s King forbids.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Say she shall be a high and mighty queen.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: To vail the title, as her mother doth.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Say I will love her everlastingly.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: But how long shall that title “ever” last?

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Sweetly in force unto her fair life’s end.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: But how long fairly shall her sweet life last?

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: As long as heaven and nature lengthens it.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: As long as hell and Richard likes of it.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Say I, her sovereign, am her subject low.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: But she, your subject, loathes such sovereignty.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Be eloquent in my behalf to her.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: An honest tale speeds best being plainly told.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Then plainly to her tell my loving tale.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Plain and not honest is too harsh a style.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Your reasons are too shallow and too quick.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: O no, my reasons are too deep and dead—

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Too deep and dead, poor infants, in their graves.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Harp not on that string, madam; that is past.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Harp on it still shall I till heart-strings break.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Now, by my George, my Garter, and my crown—

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Profaned, dishonoured, and the third usurped.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: I swear—

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: By nothing, for this is no oath.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Thy George, profaned, hath lost his lordly honour;

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Thy Garter, blemished, pawned his knightly virtue;

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Thy crown, usurped, disgraced his kingly glory.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: If something thou wouldst swear to be believed,

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Swear then by something that thou hast not wronged.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Now, by the world—

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: ’Tis full of thy foul wrongs.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: My father’s death—

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Thy life hath that dishonoured.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Then, by myself—

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Thyself is self-misused.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Why, then, by God—

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: God’s wrong is most of all.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: If thou didst fear to break an oath with Him,

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: The unity the King my husband made

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Thou hadst not broken, nor my brothers died.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: If thou hadst feared to break an oath by Him,

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Th’ imperial metal circling now thy head

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Had graced the tender temples of my child,

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: And both the Princes had been breathing here,

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Which now, two tender bedfellows for dust,

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Thy broken faith hath made a prey for worms.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: What canst thou swear by now?

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: The time to come.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: That thou hast wronged in the time o’erpast;

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: For I myself have many tears to wash

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Hereafter time, for time past wronged by thee.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: The children live whose fathers thou hast slaughtered,

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Ungoverned youth, to wail it in their age;

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: The parents live whose children thou hast butchered,

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Old barren plants, to wail it with their age.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Swear not by time to come, for that thou hast

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Misused ere used, by times ill-used o’erpast.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: As I intend to prosper and repent,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: So thrive I in my dangerous affairs

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Of hostile arms! Myself myself confound!

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Heaven and fortune bar me happy hours!

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Day, yield me not thy light, nor, night, thy rest!

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Be opposite all planets of good luck

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: To my proceeding if with dear heart’s love,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Immaculate devotion, holy thoughts,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: I tender not thy beauteous princely daughter.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: In her consists my happiness and thine;

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Without her follows to myself and thee,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Herself, the land, and many a Christian soul,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Death, desolation, ruin, and decay.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: It cannot be avoided but by this;

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: It will not be avoided but by this.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Therefore, dear mother—I must call you so—

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Be the attorney of my love to her;

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Plead what I will be, not what I have been;

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Not my deserts, but what I will deserve.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Urge the necessity and state of times,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: And be not peevish found in great designs.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Shall I be tempted of the devil thus?

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Ay, if the devil tempt you to do good.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Shall I forget myself to be myself?

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Ay, if your self’s remembrance wrong yourself.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Yet thou didst kill my children.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: But in your daughter’s womb I bury them,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Where, in that nest of spicery, they will breed

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Selves of themselves, to your recomforture.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: Shall I go win my daughter to thy will?

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: And be a happy mother by the deed.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: I go. Write to me very shortly,

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
lines.text: And you shall understand from me her mind.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Bear her my true love’s kiss; and so, farewell.
[_Kissing her. Exit Queen Elizabeth._]

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Relenting fool, and shallow, changing woman!
Enter Ratcliffe.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: How now, what news?

lines.speaker: RATCLIFFE
lines.text: Most mighty sovereign, on the western coast

lines.speaker: RATCLIFFE
lines.text: Rideth a puissant navy; to our shores

lines.speaker: RATCLIFFE
lines.text: Throng many doubtful hollow-hearted friends,

lines.speaker: RATCLIFFE
lines.text: Unarmed, and unresolved to beat them back.

lines.speaker: RATCLIFFE
lines.text: ’Tis thought that Richmond is their admiral;

lines.speaker: RATCLIFFE
lines.text: And there they hull, expecting but the aid

lines.speaker: RATCLIFFE
lines.text: Of Buckingham to welcome them ashore.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Some light-foot friend post to the Duke of Norfolk.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Ratcliffe, thyself, or Catesby. Where is he?

lines.speaker: CATESBY
lines.text: Here, my good lord.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Catesby, fly to the Duke.

lines.speaker: CATESBY
lines.text: I will my lord, with all convenient haste.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Ratcliffe, come hither. Post to Salisbury.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: When thou com’st thither—
[_To Catesby._]

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Dull, unmindful villain,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Why stay’st thou here, and go’st not to the Duke?

lines.speaker: CATESBY
lines.text: First, mighty liege, tell me your Highness’ pleasure,

lines.speaker: CATESBY
lines.text: What from your Grace I shall deliver to him.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: O, true, good Catesby. Bid him levy straight

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: The greatest strength and power that he can make,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: And meet me suddenly at Salisbury.

lines.speaker: CATESBY
lines.text: I go.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: RATCLIFFE
lines.text: What, may it please you, shall I do at Salisbury?

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Why, what wouldst thou do there before I go?

lines.speaker: RATCLIFFE
lines.text: Your Highness told me I should post before.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: My mind is changed.
Enter Stanley Earl of Derby.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Stanley, what news with you?

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: None good, my liege, to please you with the hearing;

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: Nor none so bad but well may be reported.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Hoyday, a riddle! Neither good nor bad.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: What need’st thou run so many miles about

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: When thou mayst tell thy tale the nearest way?

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Once more, what news?

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: Richmond is on the seas.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: There let him sink, and be the seas on him!

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: White-livered runagate, what doth he there?

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: I know not, mighty sovereign, but by guess.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Well, as you guess?

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: Stirred up by Dorset, Buckingham, and Morton,

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: He makes for England, here to claim the crown.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Is the chair empty? Is the sword unswayed?

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Is the King dead? The empire unpossessed?

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: What heir of York is there alive but we?

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: And who is England’s King but great York’s heir?

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Then tell me, what makes he upon the seas?

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: Unless for that, my liege, I cannot guess.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Unless for that he comes to be your liege,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: You cannot guess wherefore the Welshman comes.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Thou wilt revolt and fly to him, I fear.

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: No, my good lord; therefore mistrust me not.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Where is thy power, then, to beat him back?

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Where be thy tenants and thy followers?

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Are they not now upon the western shore,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Safe-conducting the rebels from their ships?

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: No, my good lord, my friends are in the north.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Cold friends to me. What do they in the north,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: When they should serve their sovereign in the west?

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: They have not been commanded, mighty King.

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: Pleaseth your Majesty to give me leave,

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: I’ll muster up my friends, and meet your Grace

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: Where and what time your Majesty shall please.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Ay, ay, thou wouldst be gone to join with Richmond.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: But I’ll not trust thee.

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: Most mighty sovereign,

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: You have no cause to hold my friendship doubtful.

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: I never was nor never will be false.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Go then, and muster men, but leave behind

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Your son George Stanley. Look your heart be firm,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Or else his head’s assurance is but frail.

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: So deal with him as I prove true to you.
[_Exit._]
Enter a Messenger.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: My gracious sovereign, now in Devonshire,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: As I by friends am well advertised,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Sir Edward Courtney, and the haughty prelate,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Bishop of Exeter, his elder brother,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: With many more confederates, are in arms.
Enter another Messenger.

lines.speaker: SECOND MESSENGER
lines.text: In Kent, my liege, the Guilfords are in arms,

lines.speaker: SECOND MESSENGER
lines.text: And every hour more competitors

lines.speaker: SECOND MESSENGER
lines.text: Flock to the rebels, and their power grows strong.
Enter another Messenger.

lines.speaker: THIRD MESSENGER
lines.text: My lord, the army of great Buckingham—

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Out on you, owls! Nothing but songs of death?
[_He strikes him._]

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: There, take thou that till thou bring better news.

lines.speaker: THIRD MESSENGER
lines.text: The news I have to tell your Majesty

lines.speaker: THIRD MESSENGER
lines.text: Is, that by sudden floods and fall of waters,

lines.speaker: THIRD MESSENGER
lines.text: Buckingham’s army is dispersed and scattered,

lines.speaker: THIRD MESSENGER
lines.text: And he himself wandered away alone,

lines.speaker: THIRD MESSENGER
lines.text: No man knows whither.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: I cry thee mercy.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: There is my purse to cure that blow of thine.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Hath any well-advised friend proclaimed

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Reward to him that brings the traitor in?

lines.speaker: THIRD MESSENGER
lines.text: Such proclamation hath been made, my lord.
Enter another Messenger.

lines.speaker: FOURTH MESSENGER
lines.text: Sir Thomas Lovell and Lord Marquess Dorset,

lines.speaker: FOURTH MESSENGER
lines.text: ’Tis said, my liege, in Yorkshire are in arms.

lines.speaker: FOURTH MESSENGER
lines.text: But this good comfort bring I to your Highness:

lines.speaker: FOURTH MESSENGER
lines.text: The Breton navy is dispersed by tempest.

lines.speaker: FOURTH MESSENGER
lines.text: Richmond, in Dorsetshire, sent out a boat

lines.speaker: FOURTH MESSENGER
lines.text: Unto the shore, to ask those on the banks

lines.speaker: FOURTH MESSENGER
lines.text: If they were his assistants, yea or no?—

lines.speaker: FOURTH MESSENGER
lines.text: Who answered him they came from Buckingham

lines.speaker: FOURTH MESSENGER
lines.text: Upon his party. He, mistrusting them,

lines.speaker: FOURTH MESSENGER
lines.text: Hoised sail, and made his course again for Brittany.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: March on, march on, since we are up in arms,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: If not to fight with foreign enemies,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Yet to beat down these rebels here at home.
Enter Catesby.

lines.speaker: CATESBY
lines.text: My liege, the Duke of Buckingham is taken.

lines.speaker: CATESBY
lines.text: That is the best news. That the Earl of Richmond

lines.speaker: CATESBY
lines.text: Is with a mighty power landed at Milford

lines.speaker: CATESBY
lines.text: Is colder tidings, yet they must be told.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Away towards Salisbury! While we reason here

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: A royal battle might be won and lost.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Someone take order Buckingham be brought

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: To Salisbury; the rest march on with me.
[_Flourish. Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: A Room in Lord Stanley’s house

lines.text: Enter Stanley Earl of Derby and Sir Christopher Urswick.

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: Sir Christopher, tell Richmond this from me:

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: That in the sty of the most deadly boar

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: My son George Stanley is franked up in hold;

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: If I revolt, off goes young George’s head;

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: The fear of that holds off my present aid.

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: So get thee gone. Commend me to thy lord;

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: Withal say that the Queen hath heartily consented

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: He should espouse Elizabeth her daughter.

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: But tell me, where is princely Richmond now?

lines.speaker: CHRISTOPHER
lines.text: At Pembroke, or at Ha’rfordwest in Wales.

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: What men of name resort to him?

lines.speaker: CHRISTOPHER
lines.text: Sir Walter Herbert, a renowned soldier;

lines.speaker: CHRISTOPHER
lines.text: Sir Gilbert Talbot, Sir William Stanley,

lines.speaker: CHRISTOPHER
lines.text: Oxford, redoubted Pembroke, Sir James Blunt,

lines.speaker: CHRISTOPHER
lines.text: And Rice ap Thomas, with a valiant crew,

lines.speaker: CHRISTOPHER
lines.text: And many other of great name and worth;

lines.speaker: CHRISTOPHER
lines.text: And towards London do they bend their power,

lines.speaker: CHRISTOPHER

lines.text: Well, hie thee to thy lord; I kiss his hand.

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: Farewell.
[_Exeunt._]

lines.text: Hastings, and Edward’s children, Grey, and Rivers,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Holy King Henry, and thy fair son Edward,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Vaughan, and all that have miscarried

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: By underhand, corrupted foul injustice,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: If that your moody discontented souls

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Do through the clouds behold this present hour,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Even for revenge mock my destruction.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: This is All-Souls’ day, fellow, is it not?

lines.speaker: SHERIFF
lines.text: It is.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Why, then All-Souls’ day is my body’s doomsday.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: This is the day which, in King Edward’s time,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: I wished might fall on me when I was found

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: False to his children and his wife’s allies.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: This is the day wherein I wished to fall

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: By the false faith of him whom most I trusted.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: This, this All-Souls’ day to my fearful soul

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Is the determined respite of my wrongs.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: That high All-Seer which I dallied with

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Hath turned my feigned prayer on my head

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: And given in earnest what I begged in jest.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Thus doth He force the swords of wicked men

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: To turn their own points in their masters’ bosoms.

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Thus Margaret’s curse falls heavy on my neck:

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: “When he,” quoth she, “shall split thy heart with sorrow,

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Remember Margaret was a prophetess.”

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Come lead me, officers, to the block of shame;

lines.speaker: BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: Wrong hath but wrong, and blame the due of blame.
[_Exit with Officers._]
Enter Richmond, Oxford, Blunt, Herbert, and others, with drum and colours.

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: Fellows in arms, and my most loving friends,

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: Bruised underneath the yoke of tyranny,

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: Thus far into the bowels of the land

lines.text: Have we marched on without impediment;

lines.text: And here receive we from our father Stanley

lines.text: Lines of fair comfort and encouragement.

lines.text: That spoiled your summer fields and fruitful vines,

lines.text: Swills your warm blood like wash, and makes his trough

lines.text: From Tamworth thither is but one day’s march.

lines.text: In God’s name, cheerly on, courageous friends,

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: To reap the harvest of perpetual peace

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: By this one bloody trial of sharp war.

lines.speaker: OXFORD
lines.text: Every man’s conscience is a thousand men,

lines.text: I doubt not but his friends will turn to us.

lines.text: He hath no friends but what are friends for fear,

lines.text: All for our vantage. Then in God’s name, march.

[_Exeunt._]
Enter King Richard in arms, with Norfolk, Ratcliffe  and the Earl of Surrey with others.

lines.text: My Lord of Surrey, why look you so sad?

lines.text: My heart is ten times lighter than my looks.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: My lord of Norfolk.

lines.speaker: NORFOLK
lines.text: Here, most gracious liege.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Norfolk, we must have knocks, ha, must we not?

lines.speaker: NORFOLK
lines.text: We must both give and take, my loving lord.

lines.text: Up with my tent! Here will I lie tonight.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: But where tomorrow? Well, all’s one for that.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Who hath descried the number of the traitors?

lines.speaker: NORFOLK
lines.text: Six or seven thousand is their utmost power.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Why, our battalia trebles that account.

lines.text: Besides, the King’s name is a tower of strength

lines.text: Which they upon the adverse faction want.

lines.text: Up with the tent! Come, noble gentlemen,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Let us survey the vantage of the ground.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Call for some men of sound direction;

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Let’s lack no discipline, make no delay,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD

lines.text: The weary sun hath made a golden set,

lines.text: And by the bright track of his fiery car

lines.text: Gives token of a goodly day tomorrow.

lines.text: Sir William Brandon, you shall bear my standard.

lines.text: Give me some ink and paper in my tent;

lines.text: I’ll draw the form and model of our battle,

lines.text: Limit each leader to his several charge,

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: And part in just proportion our small power.

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: My Lord of Oxford, you, Sir William Brandon,

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: And you, Sir Walter Herbert, stay with me.

lines.text: The Earl of Pembroke keeps his regiment.—

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: Good Captain Blunt, bear my goodnight to him,

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: And by the second hour in the morning

lines.text: Desire the Earl to see me in my tent.

lines.text: Yet one thing more, good captain, do for me.

lines.text: Where is Lord Stanley quartered, do you know?

lines.text: Unless I have mista’en his colours much,

lines.text: Which well I am assured I have not done,

lines.text: South from the mighty power of the King.

lines.text: If without peril it be possible,

lines.text: Sweet Blunt, make some good means to speak with him,

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: And give him from me this most needful note.

lines.text: Upon my life, my lord, I’ll undertake it;

lines.speaker: BLUNT
lines.text: And so God give you quiet rest tonight.

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: Good night, good Captain Blunt.
[_Exit Blunt._]

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: Come, gentlemen,

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: Let us consult upon tomorrow’s business;

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: Into my tent. The dew is raw and cold.
[_Richmond, Brandon Herbert, and  Oxford withdraw into the tent. The others exeunt._]

lines.text: What is’t o’clock?

lines.text: I will not sup tonight. Give me some ink and paper.

lines.text: What, is my beaver easier than it was?

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: And all my armour laid into my tent?

lines.speaker: CATESBY
lines.text: It is, my liege, and all things are in readiness.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Good Norfolk, hie thee to thy charge;

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Use careful watch; choose trusty sentinels.

lines.speaker: NORFOLK
lines.text: I go, my lord.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Stir with the lark tomorrow, gentle Norfolk.

lines.speaker: NORFOLK
lines.text: I warrant you, my lord.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Catesby!

lines.speaker: CATESBY
lines.text: My lord?

lines.text: Send out a pursuivant-at-arms

lines.text: To Stanley’s regiment. Bid him bring his power

lines.text: Before sunrising, lest his son George fall

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Into the blind cave of eternal night.
[_Exit Catesby._]

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Fill me a bowl of wine. Give me a watch.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Saddle white Surrey for the field tomorrow.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Look that my staves be sound, and not too heavy.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Ratcliffe!

lines.speaker: RATCLIFFE
lines.text: My lord?

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Saw’st thou the melancholy Lord Northumberland?

lines.speaker: RATCLIFFE
lines.text: Thomas the Earl of Surrey and himself,

lines.speaker: RATCLIFFE

lines.text: I have not that alacrity of spirit

lines.text: Nor cheer of mind that I was wont to have.

lines.text: Set it down. Is ink and paper ready?

lines.text: It is, my lord.

lines.text: Bid my guard watch; leave me.

lines.text: Fortune and victory sit on thy helm!

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: All comfort that the dark night can afford

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: Be to thy person, noble father-in-law.

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: Tell me, how fares our loving mother?

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: I, by attorney, bless thee from thy mother,

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: Who prays continually for Richmond’s good.

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: So much for that. The silent hours steal on,

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: And flaky darkness breaks within the east.

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: In brief, for so the season bids us be,

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: Prepare thy battle early in the morning,

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: And put thy fortune to the arbitrement

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: Of bloody strokes and mortal-staring war.

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: I, as I may—that which I would I cannot—

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: With best advantage will deceive the time,

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: And aid thee in this doubtful shock of arms.

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: But on thy side I may not be too forward,

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: Lest, being seen, thy brother, tender George,

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: Be executed in his father’s sight.

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: Farewell; the leisure and the fearful time

lines.text: Cuts off the ceremonious vows of love

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: And ample interchange of sweet discourse,

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: Which so-long-sundered friends should dwell upon.

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: God give us leisure for these rites of love!

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: Once more, adieu. Be valiant, and speed well.

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: Good lords, conduct him to his regiment.

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: I’ll strive with troubled thoughts to take a nap,

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: Lest leaden slumber peise me down tomorrow

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: When I should mount with wings of victory.

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: Once more, good night, kind lords and gentlemen.
[_All but Richmond leave his tent._]
[_Kneels_.]

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: O Thou, whose captain I account myself,

lines.text: Look on my forces with a gracious eye;

lines.text: Put in their hands Thy bruising irons of wrath,

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: That they may crush down with a heavy fall

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: Th’ usurping helmets of our adversaries;

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: Make us Thy ministers of chastisement,

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: That we may praise Thee in the victory.

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: To Thee I do commend my watchful soul

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: Ere I let fall the windows of mine eyes.

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: Sleeping and waking, O, defend me still!
[_Sleeps._]

[_To King Richard._]

lines.text: Let me sit heavy on thy soul tomorrow.

lines.text: Think how thou stabbed’st me in my prime of youth

lines.speaker: GHOST OF EDWARD
lines.text: At Tewksbury; despair therefore, and die!
[_To Richmond._]

lines.speaker: GHOST OF EDWARD
lines.text: Be cheerful, Richmond, for the wronged souls

lines.speaker: GHOST OF EDWARD
lines.text: Of butchered princes fight in thy behalf.

lines.speaker: GHOST OF EDWARD
lines.text: King Henry’s issue, Richmond, comforts thee.
[_Exit._]
Enter the Ghost of Henry the Sixth.
[_To King Richard._]

lines.speaker: GHOST OF HENRY
lines.text: When I was mortal, my anointed body

lines.speaker: GHOST OF HENRY
lines.text: By thee was punched full of deadly holes.

lines.speaker: GHOST OF HENRY
lines.text: Think on the Tower and me. Despair, and die;

lines.text: Harry the Sixth bids thee despair and die.
[_To Richmond._]

lines.speaker: GHOST OF HENRY
lines.text: Virtuous and holy, be thou conqueror.

lines.text: Harry, that prophesied thou shouldst be King,

lines.text: Doth comfort thee in thy sleep. Live, and flourish!
[_Exit._]
Enter the Ghost of Clarence.
[_To King Richard._]

lines.speaker: GHOST OF CLARENCE
lines.text: Let me sit heavy in thy soul tomorrow,

lines.text: I, that was washed to death with fulsome wine,

lines.text: Tomorrow in the battle think on me,

lines.speaker: GHOST OF CLARENCE
lines.text: And fall thy edgeless sword. Despair, and die!
[_To Richmond._]

lines.speaker: GHOST OF CLARENCE
lines.text: Thou offspring of the house of Lancaster,

lines.speaker: GHOST OF CLARENCE
lines.text: The wronged heirs of York do pray for thee.

lines.speaker: GHOST OF CLARENCE
lines.text: Good angels guard thy battle; live, and flourish.
[_Exit._]
Enter the Ghosts of Rivers, Grey and Vaughan.
[_To King Richard._]

lines.speaker: GHOST OF RIVERS
lines.text: Let me sit heavy in thy soul tomorrow,

lines.speaker: GHOST OF RIVERS
lines.text: Rivers that died at Pomfret. Despair and die!
[_To King Richard._]

lines.speaker: GHOST OF GREY
lines.text: Think upon Grey, and let thy soul despair!
[_To King Richard._]

lines.speaker: GHOST OF VAUGHAN
lines.text: Think upon Vaughan, and with guilty fear

lines.speaker: GHOST OF VAUGHAN
lines.text: Let fall thy lance. Despair and die!
[_To Richmond._]

lines.speaker: ALL THREE
lines.text: Awake, and think our wrongs in Richard’s bosom

lines.text: Will conquer him. Awake, and win the day.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter the Ghost of Hastings.
[_To King Richard._]

lines.speaker: GHOST OF HASTINGS
lines.text: Bloody and guilty, guiltily awake,

lines.speaker: GHOST OF HASTINGS
lines.text: And in a bloody battle end thy days.

lines.speaker: GHOST OF HASTINGS
lines.text: Think on Lord Hastings. Despair and die!
[_To Richmond._]

lines.speaker: GHOST OF HASTINGS
lines.text: Quiet untroubled soul, awake, awake.

lines.speaker: GHOST OF HASTINGS
lines.text: Arm, fight, and conquer for fair England’s sake.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: GHOSTS OF PRINCES
lines.text: Dream on thy cousins smothered in the Tower.

lines.speaker: GHOSTS OF PRINCES
lines.text: Sleep, Richmond, sleep in peace, and wake in joy;

lines.speaker: GHOSTS OF PRINCES
lines.text: Good angels guard thee from the boar’s annoy.

lines.speaker: GHOSTS OF PRINCES
lines.text: Live, and beget a happy race of kings;

lines.speaker: GHOSTS OF PRINCES

[_Exeunt._]

[_To King Richard._]

lines.speaker: GHOST OF ANNE
lines.text: Richard, thy wife, that wretched Anne thy wife,

lines.text: That never slept a quiet hour with thee,

lines.text: Now fills thy sleep with perturbations.

lines.speaker: GHOST OF ANNE
lines.text: Tomorrow in the battle think on me,

lines.speaker: GHOST OF ANNE
lines.text: And fall thy edgeless sword. Despair and die!
[_To Richmond._]

lines.speaker: GHOST OF ANNE
lines.text: Thou quiet soul, sleep thou a quiet sleep;

lines.speaker: GHOST OF ANNE
lines.text: Dream of success and happy victory.

lines.speaker: GHOST OF ANNE
lines.text: Thy adversary’s wife doth pray for thee.
[_Exit._]

[_To King Richard._]

lines.text: The first was I that helped thee to the crown;

lines.text: The last was I that felt thy tyranny.

lines.text: O, in the battle think on Buckingham,

lines.speaker: GHOST OF BUCKINGHAM
lines.text: And die in terror of thy guiltiness.

lines.text: I died for hope ere I could lend thee aid,

lines.text: But cheer thy heart, and be thou not dismayed.

[_Exit._]

lines.text: That I myself have done unto myself?

lines.text: My lord!

lines.text: Zounds! Who’s there?

lines.text: Ratcliffe, my lord; ’tis I. The early village cock

lines.speaker: RATCLIFFE
lines.text: Hath twice done salutation to the morn;

lines.speaker: RATCLIFFE
lines.text: Your friends are up and buckle on their armour.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: O Ratcliffe, I have dreamed a fearful dream!

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: What think’st thou, will our friends prove all true?

lines.speaker: RATCLIFFE
lines.text: No doubt, my lord.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: O Ratcliffe, I fear, I fear!

lines.speaker: RATCLIFFE
lines.text: Nay, good my lord, be not afraid of shadows.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: By the apostle Paul, shadows tonight

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Have struck more terror to the soul of Richard

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Than can the substance of ten thousand soldiers

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Armed in proof and led by shallow Richmond.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: ’Tis not yet near day. Come, go with me.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Under our tents I’ll play the eavesdropper,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: To see if any mean to shrink from me.
[_Exeunt Richard and Ratcliffe._]
Enter the Lords to Richmond in his tent.

lines.speaker: LORDS
lines.text: Good morrow, Richmond.

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: Cry mercy, lords and watchful gentlemen,

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: That you have ta’en a tardy sluggard here.

lines.speaker: LORDS
lines.text: How have you slept, my lord?

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: The sweetest sleep and fairest-boding dreams

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: That ever entered in a drowsy head

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: Have I since your departure had, my lords.

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: Methought their souls whose bodies Richard murdered

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: Came to my tent and cried on victory.

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: I promise you, my heart is very jocund

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: In the remembrance of so fair a dream.

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: How far into the morning is it, lords?

lines.speaker: LORDS
lines.text: Upon the stroke of four.

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: Why, then ’tis time to arm and give direction.

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: His oration to his soldiers.

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: More than I have said, loving countrymen,

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: The leisure and enforcement of the time

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: Forbids to dwell upon. Yet remember this:

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: God, and our good cause, fight upon our side;

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: The prayers of holy saints and wronged souls,

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: Like high-reared bulwarks, stand before our faces.

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: Richard except, those whom we fight against

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: Had rather have us win than him they follow.

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: For what is he they follow? Truly, gentlemen,

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: A bloody tyrant and a homicide;

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: One raised in blood, and one in blood established;

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: One that made means to come by what he hath,

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: And slaughtered those that were the means to help him;

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: A base foul stone, made precious by the foil

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: Of England’s chair, where he is falsely set;

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: One that hath ever been God’s enemy.

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: Then, if you fight against God’s enemy,

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: God will, in justice, ward you as his soldiers;

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: If you do sweat to put a tyrant down,

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: You sleep in peace, the tyrant being slain;

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: If you do fight against your country’s foes,

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: Your country’s fat shall pay your pains the hire;

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: If you do fight in safeguard of your wives,

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: Your wives shall welcome home the conquerors;

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: If you do free your children from the sword,

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: Your children’s children quits it in your age.

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: Then, in the name of God and all these rights,

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: Advance your standards, draw your willing swords.

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: For me, the ransom of my bold attempt

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: Shall be this cold corpse on the earth’s cold face;

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: But if I thrive, the gain of my attempt

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: The least of you shall share his part thereof.

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: Sound drums and trumpets boldly and cheerfully!

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: God, and Saint George! Richmond and victory!
[_Exeunt._]
Enter King Richard, Ratcliffe and Soldiers.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: What said Northumberland as touching Richmond?

lines.speaker: RATCLIFFE
lines.text: That he was never trained up in arms.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: He said the truth. And what said Surrey then?

lines.speaker: RATCLIFFE
lines.text: He smiled, and said, “The better for our purpose.”

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: He was in the right, and so indeed it is.
[_The clock striketh._]

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Tell the clock there. Give me a calendar.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Who saw the sun today?

lines.speaker: RATCLIFFE
lines.text: Not I, my lord.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Then he disdains to shine, for by the book

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: He should have braved the east an hour ago.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: A black day will it be to somebody.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Ratcliffe!

lines.speaker: RATCLIFFE
lines.text: My lord?

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: The sun will not be seen today!

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: The sky doth frown and lour upon our army.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: I would these dewy tears were from the ground.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Not shine today? Why, what is that to me

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: More than to Richmond? For the selfsame heaven

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: That frowns on me looks sadly upon him.
Enter Norfolk.

lines.speaker: NORFOLK
lines.text: Arm, arm, my lord. The foe vaunts in the field.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Come, bustle, bustle! Caparison my horse.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Call up Lord Stanley; bid him bring his power.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: I will lead forth my soldiers to the plain,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: And thus my battle shall be ordered:

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: My foreward shall be drawn out all in length,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Consisting equally of horse and foot;

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Our archers shall be placed in the midst.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: John Duke of Norfolk, Thomas Earl of Surrey,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Shall have the leading of this foot and horse.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: They thus directed, we will follow

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: In the main battle, whose puissance on either side

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Shall be well winged with our chiefest horse.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: This, and Saint George to boot! What think’st thou, Norfolk?

lines.speaker: NORFOLK
lines.text: A good direction, warlike sovereign.
[_He sheweth him a paper._]

lines.speaker: NORFOLK
lines.text: This found I on my tent this morning.
[_Reads_.]

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: “Jockey of Norfolk, be not too bold.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: For Dickon thy master is bought and sold.”

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: A thing devised by the enemy.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Go, gentlemen, every man unto his charge.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Let not our babbling dreams affright our souls;

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Conscience is but a word that cowards use,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Devised at first to keep the strong in awe.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Our strong arms be our conscience, swords our law.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: March on. Join bravely. Let us to it pell-mell,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: If not to heaven, then hand in hand to hell.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: His oration to his army.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: What shall I say more than I have inferred?

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Remember whom you are to cope withal,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: A sort of vagabonds, rascals, and runaways,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: A scum of Bretons and base lackey peasants,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Whom their o’er-cloyed country vomits forth

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: To desperate adventures and assured destruction.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: You sleeping safe, they bring to you unrest;

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: You having lands, and blessed with beauteous wives,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: They would restrain the one, distain the other.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: And who doth lead them but a paltry fellow,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Long kept in Brittany at our mother’s cost?

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: A milksop, one that never in his life

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Felt so much cold as over-shoes in snow?

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Let’s whip these stragglers o’er the seas again,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Lash hence these overweening rags of France,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: These famished beggars, weary of their lives,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Who, but for dreaming on this fond exploit,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: For want of means, poor rats, had hanged themselves.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: If we be conquered, let men conquer us,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: And not these bastard Bretons, whom our fathers

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Have in their own land beaten, bobbed, and thumped,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: And in record left them the heirs of shame.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Shall these enjoy our lands? Lie with our wives,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Ravish our daughters?
[_Drum afar off._]

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Hark, I hear their drum.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Fight, gentlemen of England! Fight, bold yeomen!

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Draw, archers, draw your arrows to the head!

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Spur your proud horses hard, and ride in blood!

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Amaze the welkin with your broken staves!
Enter a Messenger.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: What says Lord Stanley? Will he bring his power?

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: My lord, he doth deny to come.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Off with his son George’s head!

lines.speaker: NORFOLK
lines.text: My lord, the enemy is past the marsh.

lines.speaker: NORFOLK
lines.text: After the battle let George Stanley die.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: A thousand hearts are great within my bosom.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Advance our standards! Set upon our foes!

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Our ancient word of courage, fair Saint George,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Inspire us with the spleen of fiery dragons!

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Upon them! Victory sits on our helms.
[_Exeunt._]
Alarum. Excursions. Enter Norfolk and Soldiers; to him Catesby.

lines.speaker: CATESBY
lines.text: Rescue, my lord of Norfolk, rescue, rescue!

lines.speaker: CATESBY
lines.text: The King enacts more wonders than a man,

lines.speaker: CATESBY
lines.text: Daring an opposite to every danger.

lines.speaker: CATESBY
lines.text: His horse is slain, and all on foot he fights,

lines.speaker: CATESBY
lines.text: Seeking for Richmond in the throat of death.

lines.speaker: CATESBY
lines.text: Rescue, fair lord, or else the day is lost!
[_Exeunt Norfolk and Soldiers._]
Alarum. Enter King Richard.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: A horse! A horse! My kingdom for a horse!

lines.speaker: CATESBY
lines.text: Withdraw, my lord; I’ll help you to a horse.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Slave, I have set my life upon a cast,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: And I will stand the hazard of the die.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: I think there be six Richmonds in the field;

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Five have I slain today instead of him.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: A horse! A horse! My kingdom for a horse!
[_Exeunt._]

Alarum. Enter King Richard and Richmond. They fight. Richard is slain. Then retreat being sounded. Richmond exits, and Richard’s body is carried off. Flourish. Enter Richmond, Stanley Earl of Derby, bearing the crown, with other Lords and Soldiers.

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: God and your arms be praised, victorious friends!

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: The day is ours, the bloody dog is dead.

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: Courageous Richmond, well hast thou acquit thee!

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: Lo, here, this long-usurped royalty

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: From the dead temples of this bloody wretch

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: Have I plucked off, to grace thy brows withal.

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: Wear it, enjoy it, and make much of it.

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: Great God of heaven, say Amen to all!

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: But tell me, is young George Stanley living?

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: He is, my lord, and safe in Leicester town,

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: Whither, if it please you, we may now withdraw us.

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: What men of name are slain on either side?

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: John, Duke of Norfolk, Walter, Lord Ferrers,

lines.speaker: STANLEY
lines.text: Sir Robert Brakenbury, and Sir William Brandon.

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: Inter their bodies as becomes their births.

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: Proclaim a pardon to the soldiers fled

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: That in submission will return to us.

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: And then, as we have ta’en the sacrament,

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: We will unite the white rose and the red.

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: Smile heaven upon this fair conjunction,

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: That long have frowned upon their enmity.

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: What traitor hears me and says not Amen?

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: England hath long been mad, and scarred herself:

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: The brother blindly shed the brother’s blood;

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: The father rashly slaughtered his own son;

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: The son, compelled, been butcher to the sire.

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: All this divided York and Lancaster,

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: Divided in their dire division.

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: O, now let Richmond and Elizabeth,

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: The true succeeders of each royal house,

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: By God’s fair ordinance conjoin together,

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: And let their heirs, God, if Thy will be so,

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: Enrich the time to come with smoothed-faced peace,

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: With smiling plenty, and fair prosperous days.

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: Abate the edge of traitors, gracious Lord,

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: That would reduce these bloody days again,

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: And make poor England weep in streams of blood.

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: Let them not live to taste this land’s increase,

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: That would with treason wound this fair land’s peace.

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: Now civil wounds are stopped, peace lives again.

lines.speaker: RICHMOND
lines.text: That she may long live here, God say Amen.
[_Exeunt._]
